+            ExprRecord(_, _, _) => self.unported_expr("record literals (5.3b part 3)", span)
+            ExprField(_, _) => self.unported_expr("fields (5.3b part 3)", span)
+            ExprTry(_) => self.unported_expr("`?` (5.3b part 3)", span)
+            ExprAwait(inner) => self.check_await(fcx, inner, span)
+            ExprCast(_, _) => self.unsupported_expr(span, "`as` casts")
+            ExprView(_) => self.unported_expr("views (5.3b part 5)", span)
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The stub of a construct a later part of 5.3b checks: `what` is kept
+    /// as the reason N refuses the program (`unported_at`).
+    pub fn unported_expr(mut self, what: String, span: Span) -> HirExpr {
+        self.unported_at(what)
+        error_expr(span)
+    }
+
+    // `if`, with or without `else` (`check_expr`'s arm).
+    fn check_if(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        cond: Spanned<Expr>,
+        then: Spanned<Block>,
+        else_: Option<Spanned<Expr>>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let cond = self.check_expr(fcx, cond)
+        self.expect_ty(fcx, cond, TyBool, "an `if` condition")
+        let then_expr = self.check_block(fcx, then.value, then.span)
+        match else_ {
+            Some(else_branch) => {
+                let else_expr = self.check_expr(fcx, else_branch)
+                // The branches unify only when neither diverges; the `if`'s
+                // type is the branch that does not.
+                let then_d = match fcx.icx.apply(then_expr.ty) {
+                    TyNever => true
+                    _ => false
+                }
+                let else_d = match fcx.icx.apply(else_expr.ty) {
+                    TyNever => true
+                    _ => false
+                }
+                if !then_d && !else_d && !fcx.icx.unify(then_expr.ty, else_expr.ty) {
+                    self.error(
+                        "E0010",
+                        "`if` and `else` have incompatible types: `${self.show(then_expr.ty, fcx)}` vs `${self.show(else_expr.ty, fcx)}`",
+                        else_expr.span,
+                    )
+                }
+                let ty = if then_d { else_expr.ty } else { then_expr.ty }
+                HirExpr { kind: EkIf(cond, then_expr, Some(else_expr)), ty: ty, span: span }
+            }
+            None => {
+                if !fcx.icx.unify(then_expr.ty, TyUnit) {
+                    self.error(
+                        "E0010",
+                        "an `if` without `else` must have type `()`, found `${self.show(then_expr.ty, fcx)}`",
+                        then_expr.span,
+                    )
+                }
+                HirExpr { kind: EkIf(cond, then_expr, None), ty: TyUnit, span: span }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    // `inner.await` (`check_expr`'s arm): E0086 outside an async body,
+    // E0087 on what is not a future.
+    fn check_await(mut self, mut fcx: FnCtx, inner: Spanned<Expr>, span: Span) -> HirExpr {
+        let e = self.check_expr(fcx, inner)
+        if !fcx.in_async {
+            let mut d = Diagnostic::error("E0086", "`.await` is only allowed inside an `async fn`")
+            d.add_primary(self.cur_file, span, "await outside an async function")
+            d.add_note(
+                "make the enclosing function `async`, or drive the future to completion with `block_on`",
+            )
+            self.diagnostics.push(d)
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        let out = match fcx.icx.apply(e.ty) {
+            TyFuture(o) => o
+            TyError => return error_expr(span)
+            other => {
+                let mut d = Diagnostic::error(
+                    "E0087",
+                    "`.await` expects a future, found `${display_ty(other, self.defs)}`",
+                )
+                d.add_primary(self.cur_file, inner.span, "not a future")
+                self.diagnostics.push(d)
+                return error_expr(span)
+            }
+        }
+        HirExpr { kind: EkAwait(e), ty: out, span: span }
+    }
+
+    // A string with interpolation: its pieces concatenated, each hole a
+    // `String`, or a primitive turned into one (`check_interp`).
+    fn check_interp(mut self, mut fcx: FnCtx, parts: Vec<StringPart>, span: Span) -> HirExpr {
+        let mut pieces: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+        for part in parts.iter() {
+            match part {
+                StringPartLit(s) => pieces.push(
+                    HirExpr { kind: EkStrLit(s), ty: TyString, span: span },
+                )
+                StringPartExpr(e) => {
+                    let value = self.check_expr(fcx, e)
+                    match fcx.icx.apply(value.ty) {
+                        TyString => pieces.push(value)
+                        TyInt | TyFloat | TyBool | TyChar | TyError => {
+                            let part_span = value.span
+                            pieces.push(
+                                HirExpr { kind: EkToStr(value), ty: TyString, span: part_span },
+                            )
+                        }
+                        // 5.3b part 3: `try_display` looks `fmt` up as a
+                        // method, and E0013 follows when it finds none.
+                        _ => pieces.push(
+                            self.unported_expr(
+                                "interpolating a value through `Display` (5.3b part 3)",
+                                span,
+                            ),
+                        )
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        HirExpr { kind: EkStrConcat(pieces), ty: TyString, span: span }
+    }
+
+    // A path as a value: a local, a constant, a variant, `Type::Variant`
+    // (`check_path`).
+    fn check_path(mut self, mut fcx: FnCtx, path: Path, span: Span) -> HirExpr {
+        let callee_args = self.qualified_callee
+        self.qualified_callee = -1
+        let segs = path.segments
+        if segs.len() == 2 {
+            // `Type::Variant`.
+            let ty_name = segs.at(0).value
+            let v_name = segs.at(1).value
+            let def_id = self.resolve_type_in(self.cur_module, ty_name)
+            if def_id >= 0 {
+                let vi = self.variant_index(def_id, v_name)
+                if vi >= 0 { return self.make_variant(fcx, def_id, vi, Vec::new(), span) }
+                self.error("E0001", "no variant `${v_name}` on type `${ty_name}`", span)
+                return error_expr(span)
+            }
+            if self.missing_on_target(ty_name, segs.at(0).span) { return error_expr(span) }
+            self.unsupported(span, "module-qualified paths")
+            // A qualifier this module never imported, or misspelled.
+            self.name_fixes(
+                segs.at(0),
+                NeedQualifier(v_name, callee_args),
+                Vec::from_array(fcx.generics.keys()),
+            )
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        if segs.len() != 1 {
+            self.unsupported(span, "module-qualified paths")
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        let name = segs.at(0).value
+        let local = fcx.lookup(name)
+        if local >= 0 {
+            return HirExpr { kind: EkLocal(local), ty: fcx.locals.at(local).ty, span: span }
+        }
+        match self.resolve_value_in(self.cur_module, name) {
+            Some(ResDef(def_id)) => {
+                match self.kind_of(def_id) {
+                    DefKindFn(_) => {
+                        if self.sigs.at(def_id).is_none() { return error_expr(span) }
+                        // 5.3b part 3: a function as a value is a wrapper,
+                        // a closure (`make_fn_wrapper`).
+                        self.unported_expr("functions as values (5.3b part 3)", span)
+                    }
+                    DefKindConst(_) => {
+                        // A constant is a call of its function of no
+                        // argument.
+                        let ret = match self.sigs.at(def_id) {
+                            Some(s) => s.ret
+                            None => TyError
+                        }
+                        HirExpr {
+                            kind: EkCall(CalleeDef(def_id), Vec::new(), Vec::new()),
+                            ty: ret,
+                            span: span,
+                        }
+                    }
+                    _ => {
+                        self.unsupported(span, "referencing this kind of definition as a value")
+                        error_expr(span)
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            Some(ResVariant(sum_id, vi)) => self.make_variant(fcx, sum_id, vi, Vec::new(), span)
+            Some(ResBuiltin(_)) => {
+                self.unsupported(span, "using builtins as values")
+                error_expr(span)
+            }
+            None => {
+                if !self.missing_on_target(name, span) {
+                    self.error("E0001", "cannot find `${name}` in this scope", span)
+                    let nearby = fcx.visible_locals()
+                    self.name_fixes(segs.at(0), NeedValue, nearby)
+                }
+                error_expr(span)
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    // A binary operator; `&&` and `||` have nodes of their own
+    // (`check_binary`).
+    fn check_binary(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        op: BinOp,
+        lhs: Spanned<Expr>,
+        rhs: Spanned<Expr>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let logical = match op {
+            BinOpAnd => 1
+            BinOpOr => 2
+            _ => 0
+        }
+        if logical > 0 {
+            let l = self.check_expr(fcx, lhs)
+            let r = self.check_expr(fcx, rhs)
+            self.expect_ty(fcx, l, TyBool, "a logical operand")
+            self.expect_ty(fcx, r, TyBool, "a logical operand")
+            let kind = if logical == 1 { EkLogicalAnd(l, r) } else { EkLogicalOr(l, r) }
+            return HirExpr { kind: kind, ty: TyBool, span: span }
+        }
+        let l = self.check_expr(fcx, lhs)
+        let r = self.check_expr(fcx, rhs)
+        let hir_op = convert_binop(op)
+        let ty = self.binary_result_ty(fcx, hir_op, l, r, span)
+        HirExpr { kind: EkBinary(hir_op, l, r), ty: ty, span: span }
+    }
+
+    // A binary operation's type, its operands' checked: E0010 when they
+    // differ, E0013 when the operator is not defined on them
+    // (`binary_result_ty`).
+    fn binary_result_ty(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        op: HirBinOp,
+        lhs: HirExpr,
+        rhs: HirExpr,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> Ty {
+        if !fcx.icx.unify(lhs.ty, rhs.ty) {
+            self.error(
+                "E0010",
+                "mismatched operand types: `${self.show(lhs.ty, fcx)}` vs `${self.show(rhs.ty, fcx)}`",
+                span,
+            )
+            // `+` joins two `String`s only.
+            let is_add = match op {
+                OpAdd => true
+                _ => false
+            }
+            if is_add && (is_string(fcx.icx.apply(lhs.ty)) || is_string(fcx.icx.apply(rhs.ty))) {
+                let mut d = self.diagnostics.last()
+                // `$` and `{` apart, so that the note's example is no hole.
+                d.notes.push(
+                    "`+` joins two `String`s; to add any other value to a string, interpolate it: `\"$"
+                        + "{a}$"
+                        + "{b}\"`",
+                )
+            }
+            return TyError
+        }
+        let mut operand = fcx.icx.apply(lhs.ty)
+        match operand {
+            TyVar(_) => {
+                // An operand nothing constrains defaults to `Int`, as a
+                // literal does.
+                let _ = fcx.icx.unify(operand, TyInt)
+                operand = TyInt
+            }
+            _ => ()
+        }
+        match op {
+            OpAdd | OpSub | OpMul | OpDiv | OpRem => {
+                let string_add = match (op, operand) {
+                    (OpAdd, TyString) => true
+                    _ => false
+                }
+                if string_add { return TyString }
+                match operand {
+                    TyInt | TyFloat | TyNever | TyError => operand
+                    other => {
+                        self.op_not_defined(fcx, "arithmetic", other, span)
+                        TyError
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            OpLt | OpLe | OpGt | OpGe => {
+                match operand {
+                    TyInt | TyFloat | TyChar | TyNever | TyError => TyBool
+                    other => {
+                        self.op_not_defined(fcx, "comparison", other, span)
+                        TyBool
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            OpEq | OpNe => {
+                match operand {
+                    TyInt
+                        | TyFloat
+                        | TyBool
+                        | TyChar
+                        | TyString
+                        | TyUnit
+                        | TyNever
+                        | TyError => TyBool
+                    other => {
+                        self.op_not_defined(fcx, "equality", other, span)
+                        TyBool
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            OpBitAnd | OpBitOr | OpBitXor | OpShl | OpShr => {
+                match operand {
+                    TyInt | TyNever | TyError => TyInt
+                    other => {
+                        self.op_not_defined(fcx, "bitwise", other, span)
+                        TyError
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    // E0013: an operator of `kind` is not defined on `ty`
+    // (`op_not_defined`).
+    fn op_not_defined(mut self, mut fcx: FnCtx, kind: String, ty: Ty, span: Span) {
+        self.error(
+            "E0013",
+            "${kind} operators are not defined for `${self.show(ty, fcx)}` (operator traits arrive later in Phase 1)",
+            span,
+        )
+        self.note_tuple_has_no_impls(ty)
+    }
+
+    /// On the E0013 just reported, when `ty` is a tuple, why
+    /// (`note_tuple_has_no_impls`).
+    pub fn note_tuple_has_no_impls(mut self, ty: Ty) {
+        match ty {
+            TyTuple(_) => {
+                if !self.diagnostics.is_empty() {
+                    let mut d = self.diagnostics.last()
+                    d.notes.push(TUPLE_HAS_NO_IMPLS)
+                }
+            }
+            _ => ()
+        }
+    }
+
+    // A unary operator (`check_unary`).
+    fn check_unary(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        op: UnOp,
+        inner: Spanned<Expr>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let value = self.check_expr(fcx, inner)
+        let (hir_op, ty) = match op {
+            UnOpNeg => {
+                let t = fcx.icx.apply(value.ty)
+                let t = match t {
+                    TyVar(_) => {
+                        let _ = fcx.icx.unify(t, TyInt)
+                        TyInt
+                    }
+                    TyInt | TyFloat | TyNever | TyError => t
+                    other => {
+                        self.op_not_defined(fcx, "negation", other, span)
+                        TyError
+                    }
+                }
+                (OpNeg, t)
+            }
+            UnOpNot => {
+                self.expect_ty(fcx, value, TyBool, "the `!` operator")
+                (OpNot, TyBool)
+            }
+            UnOpBitNot => {
+                self.expect_ty(fcx, value, TyInt, "the `~` operator")
+                (OpBitNot, TyInt)
+            }
+            _ => {
+                self.unsupported(span, "reference operators")
+                return error_expr(span)
+            }
+        }
+        HirExpr { kind: EkUnary(hir_op, value), ty: ty, span: span }
+    }
+
+    // An array literal: its elements share a type (`check_array_literal`).
+    fn check_array_literal(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        elems: Vec<Spanned<Expr>>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let elem_ty = fcx.icx.fresh()
+        let mut checked: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+        for e in elems.iter() {
+            let v = self.check_expr(fcx, e)
+            if !fcx.icx.unify(v.ty, elem_ty) {
+                self.error(
+                    "E0010",
+                    "array elements must share a type: expected `${self.show(elem_ty, fcx)}`, found `${self.show(v.ty, fcx)}`",
+                    e.span,
+                )
+            }
+            checked.push(v)
+        }
+        HirExpr { kind: EkMakeArray(checked), ty: TyArray(elem_ty), span: span }
+    }
+
+    // `[init; n]`: the element type is `init`'s, `n` an `Int`
+    // (`check_array_repeat`).
+    fn check_array_repeat(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        init: Spanned<Expr>,
+        len: Spanned<Expr>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let init_hir = self.check_expr(fcx, init)
+        let len_hir = self.check_expr(fcx, len)
+        self.expect_ty(fcx, len_hir, TyInt, "an array length")
+        let elem_ty = fcx.icx.apply(init_hir.ty)
+        HirExpr { kind: EkArrayRepeat(init_hir, len_hir), ty: TyArray(elem_ty), span: span }
+    }
+
+    // `target[index]` (`check_index`).
+    fn check_index(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        target: Spanned<Expr>,
+        index: Spanned<Expr>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let arr = self.check_expr(fcx, target)
+        let idx = self.check_expr(fcx, index)
+        self.expect_ty(fcx, idx, TyInt, "an array index")
+        let elem_ty = fcx.icx.fresh()
+        if !fcx.icx.unify(arr.ty, TyArray(elem_ty)) {
+            self.error(
+                "E0014",
+                "cannot index a value of type `${self.show(arr.ty, fcx)}`",
+                target.span,
+            )
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        HirExpr { kind: EkIndex(arr, idx), ty: elem_ty, span: span }
+    }
+
+    /// E0010 unless `expr`'s type unifies with `expected`, `what` naming
+    /// the place (`expect_ty`).
+    pub fn expect_ty(mut self, mut fcx: FnCtx, expr: HirExpr, expected: Ty, what: String) {
+        if !fcx.icx.unify(expr.ty, expected) {
+            self.error(
+                "E0010",
+                "${what} must have type `${self.show(expected, fcx)}`, found `${self.show(expr.ty, fcx)}`",
+                expr.span,
+            )
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// A type as a diagnostic shows it, the substitution applied (`show`).
+    pub fn show(self, ty: Ty, mut fcx: FnCtx) -> String { display_ty(fcx.icx.apply(ty), self.defs) }
+
+    /// E0900 for `what`, and the error expression (`unsupported_expr`).
+    pub fn unsupported_expr(mut self, span: Span, what: String) -> HirExpr {
+        self.unsupported(span, what)
+        error_expr(span)
+    }
+}
+
+/// A literal's node (`lit_expr`).
+pub fn lit_expr(lit: Literal, span: Span) -> HirExpr {
+    match lit {
+        LiteralInt(v) => HirExpr { kind: EkIntLit(v), ty: TyInt, span: span }
+        LiteralFloat(v) => HirExpr { kind: EkFloatLit(v), ty: TyFloat, span: span }
+        LiteralStr(v) => HirExpr { kind: EkStrLit(v), ty: TyString, span: span }
+        LiteralChar(v) => HirExpr { kind: EkCharLit(v), ty: TyChar, span: span }
+        LiteralBool(v) => HirExpr { kind: EkBoolLit(v), ty: TyBool, span: span }
+    }
+}
+
+/// The node an error leaves: `()` of the error type (`error_expr`).
+pub fn error_expr(span: Span) -> HirExpr { HirExpr { kind: EkUnit, ty: TyError, span: span } }
+
+fn is_string(t: Ty) -> Bool {
+    match t {
+        TyString => true
+        _ => false
+    }
+}
+
+/// An AST binary operator as HIR's (`convert_binop`); `&&` and `||` never
+/// reach it.
+pub fn convert_binop(op: BinOp) -> HirBinOp {
+    match op {
+        BinOpAdd => OpAdd
+        BinOpSub => OpSub
+        BinOpMul => OpMul
+        BinOpDiv => OpDiv
+        BinOpRem => OpRem
+        BinOpEq => OpEq
+        BinOpNe => OpNe
+        BinOpLt => OpLt
+        BinOpLe => OpLe
+        BinOpGt => OpGt
+        BinOpGe => OpGe
+        BinOpBitAnd => OpBitAnd
+        BinOpBitOr => OpBitOr
+        BinOpBitXor => OpBitXor
+        BinOpShl => OpShl
+        BinOpShr => OpShr
+        BinOpAnd => OpEq
+        BinOpOr => OpEq
+    }
+}
````

 // The program of the module `source`, resolved natively with no std
 // module, its items and its bodies checked.
-fn check_bodies_of(source: String) -> Checker {
+pub fn check_bodies_of(source: String) -> Checker {

diff --git a/selfhost/src/typeck_member_tests.nova b/selfhost/src/typeck_member_tests.nova
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..7a30d7c6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/selfhost/src/typeck_member_tests.nova
@@ -0,0 +1,195 @@
+// N's own tests of the bodies' members (5.3b part 3): method lookup, `?`,
+// closures and functions as values (their ids, names and captures), and
+// places and mutability with their fixes, each expected value what S0's
+// `nova check --dump-hir` gives for the same source. The sources need no
+// std (typeck_body_tests.nova's `check_bodies_of`), so a `?` meets the
+// program's own `Option`. The differential compares every other input.
+//
+// They live in `src/`, imported by `main.nova`, for the reason
+// lexer_tests.nova gives.
+
+import diagnostic
+import hir
+import token
+import typeck
+import typeck_body
+import typeck_body_tests
+
+// Each diagnostic's code, message and primary span, its notes, and each
+// fix's title and edits, one a line.
+fn report(c: Checker) -> String {
+    let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new()
+    for d in c.diagnostics.iter() {
+        let at = d.labels.at(0).span
+        out.push("${d.code} ${d.message} ${at.start}..${at.end}")
+        for n in d.notes.iter() { out.push("  note: ${n}") }
+        for f in d.fixes.iter() {
+            out.push("  fix: ${f.title}")
+            for e in f.edits.iter() { out.push("    ${e.span.start}..${e.span.end} `${e.text}`") }
+        }
+    }
+    "\n".join(out.to_array())
+}
+
+// --- Method lookup ---
+
+@test
+fn an_inherent_method_comes_before_a_trait_method_of_its_name() {
+    let c = check_bodies_of(
+        "trait T { fn m(self) -> Int }\nrecord P { x: Int }\nimpl T for P { fn m(self) -> Int { 1 } }\nimpl P { fn m(self) -> Int { 2 } }\nfn f(p: P) -> Int { p.m() }\n",
+    )
+    assert(c.diagnostics.is_empty(), report(c))
+    let f = c.functions.at(0)
+    assert(f.name == "f", "the first function is `f`")
+    let call = match f.body.kind {
+        EkBlock(_, Some(t)) => t
+        _ => return assert(false, "a block with a tail")
+    }
+    match call.kind {
+        EkCall(CalleeDef(id), _, args) => {
+            assert(c.name_of(id) == "P.m", "the inherent method, `${c.name_of(id)}`")
+            assert(args.len() == 1, "the receiver its first argument")
+        }
+        _ => assert(false, "a direct call")
+    }
+}
+
+@test
+fn a_call_through_a_bound_is_a_trait_call_on_the_parameter() {
+    let c = check_bodies_of(
+        "trait T { fn m(self) -> Int\n fn z() -> Self }\nfn f<A: T>(a: A) -> Int { a.m() }\nfn g<A: T>() -> A { A::z() }\n",
+    )
+    assert(c.diagnostics.is_empty(), report(c))
+    for k in 0..2 {
+        let body = match c.functions.at(k).body.kind {
+            EkBlock(_, Some(t)) => t
+            _ => return assert(false, "a block with a tail")
+        }
+        match body.kind {
+            EkTraitCall(_, method, self_ty, _, receiver, _) => {
+                assert(method == k, "the trait's method ${k}")
+                assert(ty_eq(self_ty, TyParam(0)), "`Self` is the parameter")
+                assert(receiver.is_some() == (k == 0), "a receiver only for `a.m()`")
+            }
+            _ => assert(false, "a trait call")
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+@test
+fn a_missing_or_ambiguous_method_is_reported_with_its_fix() {
+    let c = check_bodies_of(
+        "trait A { fn go(self) }\ntrait B { fn go(self) }\nrecord P { x: Int }\nimpl A for P { fn go(self) {} }\nimpl B for P { fn go(self) {} }\nimpl P { fn length(self) -> Int { 1 } }\nfn f(p: P) {\n    p.go()\n    p.lenght()\n    p.y\n    [1].len(2)\n}\n",
+    )
+    let want = [
+        "E0015 ambiguous method call `go`: more than one trait in scope provides it 191..193",
+        "E0014 no method `lenght` on type `P` 202..208",
+        "  fix: change `lenght` to `length`",
+        "    202..208 `length`",
+        "E0014 no field `y` on record `P` 217..218",
+        "  fix: change `y` to `x`",
+        "    217..218 `x`",
+        "E0014 no method `len` on array type `[Int]` 227..230",
+    ]
+    assert(report(c) == "\n".join(want), report(c))
+}
+
+// --- `?` ---
+
+@test
+fn a_question_mark_on_the_programs_own_option_is_e0098() {
+    // No std: `Option` here is the program's own sum.
+    let c = check_bodies_of(
+        "type Option<T> = | Some(T) | None\nfn f(o: Option<Int>) -> Option<Int> { let v = o?\n Some(v) }\nconst C: Int = 1?\n",
+    )
+    let want = [
+        "E0098 `?` needs an `Option` or a `Result` 80..81",
+        "  note: this `Option<Int>` is the program's own type, not std's",
+        "E0098 `?` needs an `Option` or a `Result` 109..110",
+        "  note: its type is `Int`",
+    ]
+    assert(report(c) == "\n".join(want), report(c))
+}
+
+// --- Closures and functions as values ---
+
+@test
+fn closures_and_wrappers_take_ids_past_every_definition_in_the_order_met() {
+    let c = check_bodies_of(
+        "fn twice(n: Int) -> Int { n * 2 }\nfn f(k: Int) -> Int {\n    let a = |x: Int| x + k\n    let b = twice\n    let c = |y: Int| { let z = y\n a(z) + b(k) }\n    c(1)\n}\n",
+    )
+    assert(c.diagnostics.is_empty(), report(c))
+    let first = c.defs.defs.len()
+    // `twice`, `f`, then the closures and the wrapper, as they were lifted.
+    assert(c.functions.len() == 5, "five functions")
+    let a = c.functions.at(2)
+    let b = c.functions.at(3)
+    let cl = c.functions.at(4)
+    assert(a.def_id == first && a.name == "closure$" + "${first}", a.name)
+    assert(b.def_id == first + 1 && b.name == "fnval$" + "${first + 1}", b.name)
+    assert(cl.def_id == first + 2 && cl.name == "closure$" + "${first + 2}", cl.name)
+    // `a` captures `k`; the wrapper none; `c` captures `a`, `b` and `k`, in
+    // the order its body names them, ahead of its own locals.
+    assert(a.capture_count == 1 && a.locals.at(0).name == "k", "a captures k")
+    assert(b.capture_count == 0 && b.locals.at(0).name == "__a0", "the wrapper's parameter")
+    assert(cl.capture_count == 3, "c captures three")
+    let names = "${cl.locals.at(0).name} ${cl.locals.at(1).name} ${cl.locals.at(2).name} ${cl.locals.at(3).name} ${cl.locals.at(4).name}"
+    assert(names == "a b k y z", names)
+    assert(cl.takes_env && cl.params == 1, "a closure takes its environment and its parameter")
+}
+
+// --- Places and mutability ---
+
+@test
+fn assigning_through_an_immutable_binding_offers_mut_or_says_why_not() {
+    let c = check_bodies_of(
+        "record P { x: Int }\nimpl P {\n    fn grow(mut self) { self.x += 1 }\n    fn bad(self) { self.x = 0 }\n}\nfn f(p: P) {\n    let n = 1\n    n = 2\n    p.x = 3\n    p.grow()\n    P { x: 1 }.grow()\n}\n",
+    )
+    // The functions' bodies first, then the methods' (spec §4.1).
+    let want = [
+        "E0060 cannot assign to immutable variable `n` 132..137",
+        "  fix: make `n` mutable",
+        "    122..122 `mut `",
+        "E0060 cannot assign to a field of immutable `p` 142..149",
+        "  fix: make `p` mutable",
+        "    106..106 `mut `",
+        "E0060 `P.grow` mutates its receiver, but `p` is immutable 154..162",
+        "  fix: make `p` mutable",
+        "    106..106 `mut `",
+        "E0060 `P.grow` mutates its receiver, which cannot be a temporary 167..184",
+        "E0060 cannot assign to a field of immutable `self` 86..96",
+        "  note: declare the enclosing method's receiver as `mut self` to allow mutation",
+    ]
+    assert(report(c) == "\n".join(want), report(c))
+}
+
+@test
+fn a_compound_assignment_to_a_field_evaluates_its_receiver_once() {
+    let c = check_bodies_of("record P { x: Int }\nfn f(mut p: P) { p.x += 1 }\n")
+    assert(c.diagnostics.is_empty(), report(c))
+    let f = c.functions.at(0)
+    // `p` and the checker's own `__place`.
+    assert(f.locals.len() == 2 && f.locals.at(1).name == "__place", "a local of its own")
+    let set = match f.body.kind {
+        EkBlock(_, Some(t)) => t
+        _ => return assert(false, "a block with a tail")
+    }
+    match set.kind {
+        EkBlock(stmts, None) => {
+            match stmts.at(0).kind {
+                EkLet(1, _) => ()
+                _ => assert(false, "the receiver bound first")
+            }
+            match stmts.at(1).kind {
+                EkFieldSet(_, 0, value) => {
+                    match value.kind {
+                        EkBinary(OpAdd, _, _) => ()
+                        _ => assert(false, "`t.x + 1` stored")
+                    }
+                }
+                _ => assert(false, "then the field set")
+            }
+        }
+        _ => assert(false, "a block of its own")
+    }
+}
````

diff --git a/selfhost/src/fixes.nova b/selfhost/src/fixes.nova
index 50182f78..c04fb4ad 100644
--- a/selfhost/src/fixes.nova
+++ b/selfhost/src/fixes.nova
@@ -9,8 +9,9 @@
 // §3.2, ADR 0055). 5.3b adds what the bodies' unknown values need: the
 // `Need`s of a value, a call's callee and a qualifier, `STD_ONLY_PUBLIC_FORMS`,
 // `offers`, `arity`, `variant_arity`, `variant_named` and `has_member`, and
-// `Binding` (ADR 0056); the rest of fixes.rs comes with the parts that use
-// it.
+// `Binding` (ADR 0056); then a record literal's `Need`, `mutable_fix`,
+// `immutable_note`, `field_fix` and `method_fix` (5.3b part 3); the rest
+// of fixes.rs comes with the parts that use it.
 
 import ast
 import diagnostic
@@ -18,16 +19,19 @@ import hir
 import resolver
 import token
 import typeck
+import typeck_body
+import typeck_method
 
 /// What an unknown name must be at its site (`Need`): the item passes
 /// meet a type and a trait; the bodies a value, a call's callee with its
-/// argument count, and `T` in `T::member`, with the call's argument count
-/// when it is a callee's, -1 when it is not.
+/// argument count, a record literal's record, and `T` in `T::member`, with
+/// the call's argument count when it is a callee's, -1 when it is not.
 pub type Need =
     | NeedType
     | NeedTrait
     | NeedValue
     | NeedCall(Int)
+    | NeedRecord

+        let v = fcx.new_local_unscoped("__ok", payload, false, span)
+        let mut bad_binders: Vec<HirPattern> = Vec::new()
+        let mut bad_args: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+        if !is_option {
+            let err_ty = if args.len() > 1 { args.at(1) } else { TyError }
+            let x = fcx.new_local_unscoped("__err", err_ty, false, span)
+            bad_binders.push(PatBind(x))
+            bad_args.push(local_expr(x, err_ty, span))
+        }
+        let early = HirExpr { kind: EkMakeVariant(sum, bad_idx, bad_args), ty: ret, span: span }
+        let mut good_fields: Vec<HirPattern> = Vec::new()
+        good_fields.push(PatBind(v))
+        let mut arms: Vec<HirArm> = Vec::new()
+        arms.push(
+            HirArm {
+                pattern: PatVariant(sum, good_idx, good_fields),
+                guard: None,
+                body: local_expr(v, payload, span),
+                span: span,
+            },
+        )
+        arms.push(
+            HirArm {
+                pattern: PatVariant(sum, bad_idx, bad_binders),
+                guard: None,
+                body: HirExpr { kind: EkReturn(Some(early)), ty: TyNever, span: span },
+                span: span,
+            },
+        )
+        HirExpr { kind: EkMatch(value, arms), ty: payload, span: span }
+    }
+
+    // E0099: the enclosing function's return type `other` is not the sum
+    // the `?` is on (`check_try`'s arm).
+    fn try_cannot_return(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        other: Ty,
+        is_option: Bool,
+        result: Int,
+        span: Span,
+    ) {
+        let mut d = Diagnostic::error("E0099", "`?` cannot return from this function")
+        d.add_primary(self.cur_file, span, "this `?` would return early")
+        let what = if is_option { "an `Option`" } else { "a `Result`" }
+        d.add_note("the function returns `${self.show(other, fcx)}`, not ${what}")
+        let returns_result = match other {
+            TySum(id, _) => id >= 0 && id == result
             _ => false
         }
+        if is_option && returns_result {
+            d.add_note("to return an error when the value is `None`, write `.ok_or(err)?`")
+        }
+        if fcx.entry {
+            d.add_note("`main` and `@test` functions return `()`, so `?` cannot return from them")
+        }
+        match other {
+            TySum(id, _) => {
+                let n = self.name_of(id)
+                if n == "Option" || n == "Result" {
+                    d.add_note(
+                        "this `${self.show(other, fcx)}` is the program's own type, not std's",
+                    )
+                }
+            }
+            _ => ()
+        }
+        self.diagnostics.push(d)
     }
 
     // A call of the function or extern function `def_id` by name
diff --git a/selfhost/src/typeck_closure.nova b/selfhost/src/typeck_closure.nova
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..9a469050
--- /dev/null
+++ b/selfhost/src/typeck_closure.nova
@@ -0,0 +1,208 @@
+// The type checker's closures and functions as values: a port of
+// check.rs's `check_closure`, `lift_closure` and `make_fn_wrapper`,
+// function by function and with the same names (spec
+// docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-phase-5-3-the-type-checker-and-hir-design.md
+// §4.2, ADR 0056). typeck_body.nova gives the idioms and holds
+// `collect_captures` and `remap_locals`.
+//
+// A closure is lifted into a function of its own, its captures first among
+// its locals, and the closure's value is a `MakeClosure` of its id; a bare
+// function used as a value gets a wrapper, a closure of no capture that
+// calls it. Each takes the next id past every definition
+// (`fresh_closure_def`), in the order met, and is named `closure$<id>` or
+// `fnval$<id>`; the dump prints the id under ADR 0056 §3's rule.
+
+import ast
+import fixes
+import hir
+import infer
+import token
+import typeck
+import typeck_body
+import typeck_expr
+import typeck_ty
+
+impl Checker {
+    /// `|params| body`, lifted into a function of its own; the locals of
+    /// the scopes around it that its body names are captured by value
+    /// (`check_closure`).
+    pub fn check_closure(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        params: Vec<Param>,
+        ret: Option<Spanned<Type>>,
+        body: Spanned<Expr>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        // The locals below this index are the enclosing scopes', captures
+        // when the body names them.
+        let snapshot = fcx.locals.len()
+        let generics_scope = fcx.generics
+        fcx.scopes.push(Map::new())
+        let mut param_count = 0
+        let mut param_types: Vec<Ty> = Vec::new()
+        for p in params.iter() {
+            let infer = match p.ty.value {
+                TypeInfer => true
+                _ => false
+            }
+            let ty = if infer {
+                fcx.icx.fresh()
+            } else {
+                self.convert_ty(p.ty, generics_scope, fcx.param_bounds)
+            }
+            let _ = self.bind_local(fcx, p.name.value, ty, p.is_mut, p.name.span, BindingParam)
+            param_count += 1
+            param_types.push(ty)
+        }
+        let ret_ty = match ret {
+            Some(rt) => self.convert_ty(rt, generics_scope, fcx.param_bounds)
+            None => fcx.icx.fresh()
+        }
+        // A `break` or `continue` in the body cannot reach a loop around
+        // the closure; a closure is never async, so `.await` is E0086 in
+        // it; a `return` and a `?` return from the closure, whose return
+        // type a `?` constrains while it is inferred.
+        let saved_loop_depth = fcx.loop_depth
+        fcx.loop_depth = 0
+        let saved_in_async = fcx.in_async
+        fcx.in_async = false
+        let saved_ret_ty = fcx.ret_ty
+        fcx.ret_ty = ret_ty
+        let saved_entry = fcx.entry
+        fcx.entry = false
+        let saved_in_const = fcx.in_const
+        fcx.in_const = false
+        let body_hir = self.check_expr(fcx, body)
+        fcx.loop_depth = saved_loop_depth
+        fcx.in_async = saved_in_async
+        fcx.ret_ty = saved_ret_ty
+        fcx.entry = saved_entry
+        fcx.in_const = saved_in_const
+        if !fcx.icx.unify(body_hir.ty, ret_ty) {
+            self.error(
+                "E0010",
+                "closure body has type `${self.show(body_hir.ty, fcx)}` but its declared return type is `${self.show(ret_ty, fcx)}`",
+                body.span,
+            )
+        }
+        let _ = fcx.scopes.pop()
+        let closure_ty = TyFn(param_types, ret_ty)
+        self.lift_closure(fcx, snapshot, param_count, ret_ty, body_hir, closure_ty, span)
+    }
+
+    // A checked closure body made a function of its own: the captured
+    // locals become its first, the closure's own follow, renumbered; the
+    // `MakeClosure` that makes its value (`lift_closure`).
+    fn lift_closure(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        snapshot: Int,
+        param_count: Int,
+        ret_ty: Ty,
+        body: HirExpr,
+        closure_ty: Ty,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        // The locals below `snapshot` that the body names.
+        let captures: Vec<Int> = Vec::new()
+        collect_captures(body, snapshot, captures)
+        let capture_count = captures.len()
+        // Captures to 0..C, then the closure's own locals.
+        let mut remap: Map<Int, Int> = Map::new()
+        let mut new_locals: Vec<Local> = Vec::new()
+        for i in 0..captures.len() {
+            let cap = captures.at(i)
+            let _ = remap.insert(cap, i)
+            new_locals.push(copy_local(fcx.locals.at(cap)))
+        }
+        let mut old = snapshot
+        while old < fcx.locals.len() {
+            let _ = remap.insert(old, capture_count + (old - snapshot))
+            new_locals.push(copy_local(fcx.locals.at(old)))
+            old += 1
+        }
+        remap_locals(body, remap)
+        let generics = fcx.generics.len()
+        let mut type_args: Vec<Ty> = Vec::new()
+        for k in 0..generics { type_args.push(TyParam(k)) }
+        let cdef = self.fresh_closure_def()
+        let closure_fn = HirFunction {
+            def_id: cdef,
+            name: "closure$" + "${cdef}",
+            generics: generics,
+            bounds: fcx.param_bounds,
+            takes_env: true,
+            capture_count: capture_count,
+            params: param_count,
+            locals: new_locals,
+            ret_ty: ret_ty,
+            // A lifted closure's body is never async.
+            is_async: false,
+            body: body,
+            span: FileSpan { file: self.cur_file, span: span },
+        }
+        fcx.pending_closures.push(closure_fn)
+        let mut capture_exprs: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+        for c in captures.iter() {
+            capture_exprs.push(HirExpr { kind: EkLocal(c), ty: fcx.locals.at(c).ty, span: span })
+        }
+        HirExpr { kind: EkMakeClosure(cdef, type_args, capture_exprs), ty: closure_ty, span: span }
+    }
+
+    /// A bare function used as a value: a wrapper `(env, params) {
+    /// target(params) }` of no capture (`make_fn_wrapper`).
+    pub fn make_fn_wrapper(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        target: Int,
+        target_type_args: Vec<Ty>,
+        param_types: Vec<Ty>,
+        ret: Ty,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let generics = fcx.generics.len()
+        let mut type_args: Vec<Ty> = Vec::new()
+        for k in 0..generics { type_args.push(TyParam(k)) }
+        let cdef = self.fresh_closure_def()
+        let mut locals: Vec<Local> = Vec::new()
+        let mut call_args: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+        for i in 0..param_types.len() {
+            let pty = param_types.at(i)
+            locals.push(Local { name: "__a${i}", ty: pty, is_mut: false, span: span })
+            call_args.push(HirExpr { kind: EkLocal(i), ty: pty, span: span })
+        }
+        let body = HirExpr {
+            kind: EkCall(CalleeDef(target), target_type_args, call_args),
+            ty: ret,
+            span: span,
+        }
+        let wrapper = HirFunction {
+            def_id: cdef,
+            name: "fnval$" + "${cdef}",
+            generics: generics,
+            bounds: fcx.param_bounds,
+            takes_env: true,
+            capture_count: 0,
+            params: param_types.len(),
+            locals: locals,
+            ret_ty: ret,
+            // A forwarding call, never a `.await`.
+            is_async: false,
+            body: body,
+            span: FileSpan { file: self.cur_file, span: span },
+        }
+        fcx.pending_closures.push(wrapper)
+        HirExpr {
+            kind: EkMakeClosure(cdef, type_args, Vec::new()),
+            ty: TyFn(param_types, ret),
+            span: span,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+// A copy of `l`, as S0's `clone`: the lifted function's locals are its
+// own, which finalizing rewrites in place.
+fn copy_local(l: Local) -> Local {
+    Local { name: l.name, ty: l.ty, is_mut: l.is_mut, span: l.span }
+}
