````diff
diff --git a/selfhost/src/typeck_method.nova b/selfhost/src/typeck_method.nova
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..362327ac
--- /dev/null
+++ b/selfhost/src/typeck_method.nova
@@ -0,0 +1,857 @@
+// The type checker's members: a port of check.rs's `check_record_literal`,
+// `check_field`, `tuple_index_on_unknown`, `no_field_message`,
+// `record_field_index_and_ty`, `resolve_method_on`, `trait_method_index`,
+// `trait_assoc_fn_index`, `find_inherent_method`, `qualifier_self_ty`,
+// `find_trait_assoc_fns`, `check_method_call`, `check_mutable_receiver`,
+// `emit_inherent_call`, `emit_assoc_call`, `emit_trait_call`,
+// `try_display` and `shown_method`, with `MethodRes` and `TraitCallSelf`,
+// function by function and with the same names (spec
+// docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-phase-5-3-the-type-checker-and-hir-design.md
+// §4.2, ADR 0056). typeck_body.nova gives the idioms; fixes.nova's
+// `find_assoc_fns` serves this file too.
+//
+// - A field initializer's or a receiver's AST travels with its checked
+//   form where S0's does, so `place_root` can walk it (typeck_place.nova).
+// - The language server's probe and index (`probe_receiver`, `note_use`,
+//   `note_field`, `note_qualifier`, `mark_shorthand`) are not ported
+//   (decision 8).
+
+import ast
+import diagnostic
+import fixes
+import hir
+import infer
+import resolver
+import token
+import typeck
+import typeck_body
+import typeck_call
+import typeck_expr
+import typeck_place
+
+/// How a method name resolves on a receiver (`MethodRes`): an inherent
+/// method's id, a trait's method (the trait's id and the method's index),
+/// none, or more than one trait's.
+pub type MethodRes =
+    | MethodResInherent(Int)
+    | MethodResTrait(Int, Int)
+    | MethodResNone
+    | MethodResAmbiguous
+
+/// Where a trait call's `Self` comes from (`TraitCallSelf`): a receiver,
+/// checked and as written, or a qualifier's type (`Type::f`, `T::f`).
+pub type TraitCallSelf =
+    | TraitCallSelfReceiver(HirExpr, Spanned<Expr>)
+    | TraitCallSelfQualifier(Ty)
+
+impl Checker {
+    // --- Record literals ---
+
+    /// `Name { field: value, …, ..base }` (`check_record_literal`).
+    pub fn check_record_literal(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        path: Path,
+        fields: Vec<FieldInit>,
+        base: Option<Spanned<Expr>>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        if path.segments.len() != 1 {
+            self.unsupported(span, "module-qualified record paths")
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        let name = path.segments.at(0).value
+        let def_id = self.resolve_type_in(self.cur_module, name)
+        if def_id < 0 {
+            if !self.missing_on_target(name, path.segments.at(0).span) {
+                self.error("E0001", "cannot find record `${name}`", span)
+                self.name_fixes(path.segments.at(0), NeedRecord, Vec::new())
+            }
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        let mut found: Option<RecordType> = None
+        for r in self.records.iter() {
+            if r.def_id == def_id {
+                found = Some(r)
+                break
+            }
+        }
+        let rec = match found {
+            Some(r) => r
+            None => {
+                self.error("E0010", "`${name}` is not a record type", span)
+                return error_expr(span)
+            }
+        }
+        let mut type_args: Vec<Ty> = Vec::new()
+        for _ in 0..rec.generics { type_args.push(fcx.icx.fresh()) }
+        let record_ty = TyRecord(def_id, type_args)
+        // The initializers into locals in source order, then the base, so
+        // their effects come left to right; the slots are then filled from
+        // them in declaration order.
+        let mut stmts: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+        let mut provided: Map<String, Int> = Map::new()
+        for init in fields.iter() {
+            let fname = init.name.value
+            let mut field: Option<HirField> = None
+            for f in rec.fields.iter() {
+                if f.name == fname {
+                    field = Some(f)
+                    break
+                }
+            }
+            let field = match field {
+                Some(f) => f
+                None => {
+                    self.error("E0014", "record `${name}` has no field `${fname}`", init.name.span)
+                    let mut candidates: Vec<String> = Vec::new()
+                    for f in rec.fields.iter() {
+                        let mut given = false
+                        for g in fields.iter() { if g.name.value == f.name { given = true } }
+                        if !given { candidates.push(f.name) }
+                    }
+                    let fix = change_to(self.cur_file, init.name, candidates.to_array())
+                    self.push_fix(fix)
+                    continue
+                }
+            }
+            // Normalization seam: a field may declare a projection on the
+            // record's own bounded parameter, which an earlier field's value
+            // may have made concrete.
+            let expected = self.instantiate(field.ty, type_args, fcx.icx, init.name.span)
+            let value = match init.value {
+                Some(v) => self.check_expr(fcx, v)
+                // Shorthand `{ x }` binds the local named `x`.
+                None => {
+                    let mut segments: Vec<Spanned<String>> = Vec::new()
+                    segments.push(init.name)
+                    self.check_path(fcx, Path { segments: segments }, init.name.span)
+                }
+            }
+            if !fcx.icx.unify(value.ty, expected) {
+                self.error(
+                    "E0010",
+                    "field `${fname}` expects `${self.show(expected, fcx)}` but found `${self.show(value.ty, fcx)}`",
+                    init.name.span,
+                )
+            }
+            let local = fcx.new_local("__f_${fname}", value.ty, false, init.name.span)
+            stmts.push(HirExpr { kind: EkLet(local, value), ty: TyUnit, span: span })
+            if provided.insert(fname, local).is_some() {
+                self.error("E0014", "field `${fname}` specified more than once", init.name.span)
+            }
+        }
+        // A `..base` fills the fields not given, bound to a local so that it
+        // is evaluated once, after the fields.
+        let base_local = match base {
+            Some(base_expr) => {
+                let checked = self.check_expr(fcx, base_expr)
+                if !fcx.icx.unify(checked.ty, record_ty) {
+                    self.error(
+                        "E0010",
+                        "the `..` base has type `${self.show(checked.ty, fcx)}` but `${name}` was expected",
+                        base_expr.span,
+                    )
+                }
+                let local = fcx.new_local("__base", record_ty, false, span)
+                stmts.push(HirExpr { kind: EkLet(local, checked), ty: TyUnit, span: span })
+                local
+            }
+            None => -1
+        }
+        // The slots in declaration order, from the evaluated locals.
+        let mut ordered: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+        let mut missing: Vec<String> = Vec::new()
+        for idx in 0..rec.fields.len() {
+            let field = rec.fields.at(idx)
+            // The same seam, defence in depth (S0's comment).
+            let field_ty = self.instantiate(field.ty, type_args, fcx.icx, span)
+            match provided.get(field.name) {
+                Some(local) => ordered.push(
+                    HirExpr { kind: EkLocal(local), ty: field_ty, span: span },
+                )
+                None => {
+                    if base_local >= 0 {
+                        let target = HirExpr {
+                            kind: EkLocal(base_local),
+                            ty: record_ty,
+                            span: span,
+                        }
+                        ordered.push(
+                            HirExpr { kind: EkFieldGet(target, idx), ty: field_ty, span: span },
+                        )
+                    } else {
+                        missing.push("`${field.name}`")
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        if !missing.is_empty() {
+            let mut list = ""
+            for k in 0..missing.len() {
+                if k > 0 { list = list + ", " }
+                list = list + missing.at(k)
+            }
+            self.error("E0014", "missing field(s) in `${name}`: ${list}", span)
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        let make = HirExpr { kind: EkMakeRecord(def_id, ordered), ty: record_ty, span: span }
+        if stmts.is_empty() {
+            make
+        } else {
+            HirExpr { kind: EkBlock(stmts, Some(make)), ty: record_ty, span: span }
+        }
+    }
+
+    // --- Fields ---
+
+    /// `target.field` (`check_field`).
+    pub fn check_field(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        target: Spanned<Expr>,
+        field: Spanned<String>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let recv = self.check_expr(fcx, target)
+        let recv_ty = fcx.icx.apply(recv.ty)
+        // An unfinished `x.` has an empty name, which the parser reported.
+        if field.value == "" { return error_expr(span) }
+        match self.record_field_index_and_ty(fcx, recv_ty, field.value, span) {
+            Some((index, field_ty)) => return HirExpr {
+                kind: EkFieldGet(recv, index),
+                ty: field_ty,
+                span: span,
+            }
+            None => ()
+        }
+        // A broken receiver reported its own error.
+        match recv_ty {
+            TyError => return error_expr(span)
+            _ => ()
+        }
+        if self.tuple_index_on_unknown(fcx, recv_ty, field) { return error_expr(span) }
+        self.error("E0014", self.no_field_message(fcx, recv_ty, field.value), field.span)
+        let fix = self.field_fix(recv_ty, field)
+        self.push_fix(fix)
+        error_expr(span)
+    }
+
+    /// `t.N` on a value whose type is not yet known: E0011, and `true`;
+    /// `false` for any other field or receiver (`tuple_index_on_unknown`).
+    pub fn tuple_index_on_unknown(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        recv_ty: Ty,
+        field: Spanned<String>,
+    ) -> Bool {
+        let mut is_index = true
+        for k in 0..field.value.byte_len() {
+            let b = field.value.byte_at(k)
+            if b < 48 || b > 57 { is_index = false }
+        }
+        let unknown = match fcx.icx.apply(recv_ty) {
+            TyVar(_) => true
+            _ => false
+        }
+        if !is_index || !unknown { return false }
+        self.error(
+            "E0011",
+            "the type of this value must be known before `.${field.value}` reads an element of it",
+            field.span,
+        )
+        let mut d = self.diagnostics.last()
+        d.notes.push("annotate the value's type, for example `let p: (Int, Int) = …`")
+        // Bound to the error type, so that the variable is not reported
+        // again as one inference could not solve.
+        let _ = fcx.icx.unify(recv_ty, TyError)
+        true
+    }
+
+    /// The "no such field" message for a receiver type that is not the
+    /// error type (`no_field_message`).
+    pub fn no_field_message(self, mut fcx: FnCtx, recv_ty: Ty, field_name: String) -> String {
+        let mut record_name: Option<String> = None
+        match recv_ty {
+            TyRecord(def_id, _) => {
+                for r in self.records.iter() {
+                    if r.def_id == def_id {
+                        record_name = Some(r.name)
+                        break
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            _ => ()
+        }
+        match record_name {
+            Some(n) => return "no field `${field_name}` on record `${n}`"
+            None => ()
+        }
+        match fcx.icx.apply(recv_ty) {
+            // `t.2` on `(Int, Int)`, or `t.x` on a tuple.
+            TyTuple(_) => "no field `${field_name}` on `${self.show(recv_ty, fcx)}`"
+            _ => "cannot access field `${field_name}` on `${self.show(recv_ty, fcx)}`"
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// A field of a record type, or an element of a tuple type: its index
+    /// and its type, instantiated; `None` when there is no such field
+    /// (`record_field_index_and_ty`).
+    pub fn record_field_index_and_ty(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        recv_ty: Ty,
+        field: String,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> Option<(Int, Ty)> {
+        let resolved = fcx.icx.apply(recv_ty)
+        let (def_id, args) = match resolved {
+            TyTuple(elems) => {
+                // `t.N`: the parser lets only decimal digits through.
+                let index = parse_index(field)
+                if index < 0 || index >= elems.len() { return None }
+                return Some((index, elems.at(index)))
+            }
+            TyRecord(d, a) => (d, a)
+            _ => return None
+        }
+        let mut found: Option<RecordType> = None
+        for r in self.records.iter() {
+            if r.def_id == def_id {
+                found = Some(r)
+                break
+            }
+        }
+        let rec = found?
+        let mut index = -1
+        for k in 0..rec.fields.len() {
+            if rec.fields.at(k).name == field {
+                index = k
+                break
+            }
+        }
+        if index < 0 { return None }
+        // Normalization seam: the field's type in this instantiation's
+        // arguments, its projections resolved.
+        let field_ty = self.instantiate(rec.fields.at(index).ty, args, fcx.icx, span)
+        Some((index, field_ty))
+    }
+
+    // --- Method lookup ---
+
+    /// A method `name` on a receiver of the resolved type `recv_ty`, with no
+    /// diagnostic (`resolve_method_on`).
+    pub fn resolve_method_on(self, recv_ty: Ty, fcx: FnCtx, name: String) -> MethodRes {
+        let mut matches: Vec<(Int, Int)> = Vec::new()
+        match recv_ty {
+            TyParam(k) => {
+                if k < fcx.param_bounds.len() {
+                    for tid in fcx.param_bounds.at(k).iter() {
+                        let i = self.trait_method_index(tid, name)
+                        if i >= 0 { matches.push((tid, i)) }
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            _ => {
+                let h = match head(recv_ty) {
+                    Some(h) => h
+                    None => return MethodResNone
+                }
+                // Inherent methods first, but only an impl that fits the
+                // receiver counts.
+                let def = self.find_inherent_method(recv_ty, h, name)
+                if def >= 0 { return MethodResInherent(def) }
+                for imp in self.impls.iter() {
+                    if !head_eq(imp.self_head, h) || match_args(imp, recv_ty).is_none() { continue }
+                    if imp.trait_id < 0 { continue }
+                    let idx = self.trait_method_index(imp.trait_id, name)
+                    if idx >= 0 { matches.push((imp.trait_id, idx)) }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        if matches.len() == 0 {
+            MethodResNone
+        } else if matches.len() == 1 {
+            let (t, i) = matches.at(0)
+            MethodResTrait(t, i)
+        } else {
+            MethodResAmbiguous
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The index of trait `trait_id`'s method `name` that takes a `self`
+    /// receiver, or -1 (`trait_method_index`).
+    pub fn trait_method_index(self, trait_id: Int, name: String) -> Int {
+        for t in self.traits.iter() {
+            if t.def_id == trait_id {
+                for k in 0..t.methods.len() {
+                    let m = t.methods.at(k)
+                    if m.name == name && m.has_self { return k }
+                }
+                return -1
+            }
+        }
+        -1
+    }
+
+    /// The index of trait `trait_id`'s associated function `name`, one with
+    /// no `self` receiver, or -1 (`trait_assoc_fn_index`).
+    pub fn trait_assoc_fn_index(self, trait_id: Int, name: String) -> Int {
+        for t in self.traits.iter() {
+            if t.def_id == trait_id {
+                for k in 0..t.methods.len() {
+                    let m = t.methods.at(k)
+                    if m.name == name && !m.has_self { return k }
+                }
+                return -1
+            }
+        }
+        -1
+    }
+
+    /// The method `name` of the first inherent impl of `h` that fits
+    /// `recv_ty`, an associated function skipped, or -1
+    /// (`find_inherent_method`).
+    pub fn find_inherent_method(self, recv_ty: Ty, h: TyHead, name: String) -> Int {
+        for imp in self.impls.iter() {
+            if imp.trait_id >= 0 || !head_eq(imp.self_head, h) { continue }
+            if match_args(imp, recv_ty).is_none() { continue }
+            for (n, d) in imp.methods.iter() { if n == name && !self.selfless.at(d) { return d } }
+        }
+        -1
+    }
+
+    /// The self type a two-segment path's qualifier names (`Int::zero()`,
+    /// `P::new()`, `Box::make(…)`), a generic type's arguments fresh
+    /// variables (`qualifier_self_ty`).
+    pub fn qualifier_self_ty(self, mut fcx: FnCtx, name: String) -> Option<Ty> {
+        if name == "Int" { return Some(TyInt) }
+        if name == "Float" { return Some(TyFloat) }
+        if name == "Bool" { return Some(TyBool) }
+        if name == "Char" { return Some(TyChar) }
+        if name == "String" { return Some(TyString) }
+        if name == "Bytes" { return Some(TyBytes) }
+        // `Future` carries no associated functions.
+        if name == "Future" { return None }
+        let def_id = self.resolve_type_in(self.cur_module, name)
+        if def_id < 0 { return None }
+        let arity = self.type_arity.at(def_id)
+        let mut args: Vec<Ty> = Vec::new()
+        for _ in 0..arity { args.push(fcx.icx.fresh()) }
+        match self.kind_of(def_id) {
+            DefKindRecord(_) => Some(TyRecord(def_id, args))
+            DefKindSum(_, _) => Some(TySum(def_id, args))
+            _ => None
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Every associated function `name` reachable through a trait impl that
+    /// fits `self_ty` (`find_trait_assoc_fns`).
+    pub fn find_trait_assoc_fns(self, self_ty: Ty, name: String) -> Vec<(Int, Int)> {
+        let mut out: Vec<(Int, Int)> = Vec::new()
+        let h = match head(self_ty) {
+            Some(h) => h
+            None => return out
+        }
+        for imp in self.impls.iter() {
+            if !head_eq(imp.self_head, h) || match_args(imp, self_ty).is_none() { continue }
+            if imp.trait_id < 0 { continue }
+            let idx = self.trait_assoc_fn_index(imp.trait_id, name)
+            if idx >= 0 { out.push((imp.trait_id, idx)) }
+        }
+        out
+    }
+
+    // --- Method calls ---
+
+    /// `receiver.method(args)`, the receiver and the arguments checked;
+    /// `receiver_ast` is the receiver as written, for `place_root`
+    /// (`check_method_call`).
+    pub fn check_method_call(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        receiver: HirExpr,
+        receiver_ast: Spanned<Expr>,
+        method: Spanned<String>,
+        args: Vec<HirExpr>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let recv_ty = fcx.icx.apply(receiver.ty)
+        match recv_ty {
+            TyError => return error_expr(span)
+            TyVar(_) => {
+                self.error(
+                    "E0011",
+                    "cannot infer the receiver's type; add a type annotation",
+                    receiver.span,
+                )
+                return error_expr(span)
+            }
+            // An array's built-in `len`, then the methods of its impls.
+            TyArray(_) => {
+                if method.value == "len" && args.is_empty() {
+                    return HirExpr { kind: EkArrayLen(receiver), ty: TyInt, span: span }
+                }
+                match self.resolve_method_on(recv_ty, fcx, method.value) {
+                    MethodResNone => {
+                        self.error(
+                            "E0014",
+                            "no method `${method.value}` on array type `${self.show(recv_ty, fcx)}`",
+                            method.span,
+                        )
+                        let fix = self.method_fix(recv_ty, fcx, method)
+                        self.push_fix(fix)
+                        return error_expr(span)
+                    }
+                    _ => ()
+                }
+            }
+            _ => ()
+        }
+        match self.resolve_method_on(recv_ty, fcx, method.value) {
+            MethodResInherent(def_id) => {
+                self.check_mutable_receiver(fcx, def_id, receiver_ast, span)
+                self.emit_inherent_call(fcx, def_id, receiver, args, span)
+            }
+            MethodResTrait(trait_id, method_idx) => self.emit_trait_call(
+                fcx,
+                trait_id,
+                method_idx,
+                TraitCallSelfReceiver(receiver, receiver_ast),
+                args,
+                span,
+            )
+            MethodResAmbiguous => {
+                self.error(
+                    "E0015",
+                    "ambiguous method call `${method.value}`: more than one trait in scope provides it",
+                    method.span,
+                )
+                error_expr(span)
+            }
+            MethodResNone => {
+                self.error(
+                    "E0014",
+                    "no method `${method.value}` on type `${self.show(recv_ty, fcx)}`",
+                    method.span,
+                )
+                let fix = self.method_fix(recv_ty, fcx, method)
+                self.push_fix(fix)
+                error_expr(span)
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    // A method declaring `mut self` needs its receiver reachable through a
+    // mutable binding (`check_mutable_receiver`).
+    fn check_mutable_receiver(
+        mut self,
+        fcx: FnCtx,
+        def_id: Int,
+        receiver_ast: Spanned<Expr>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) {
+        if !self.mut_self.at(def_id) { return }
+        let mname = self.shown_method(def_id)
+        self.require_mutable_place(fcx, receiver_ast, span, MutTargetReceiver(mname))
+    }
+
+    // An inherent method's call, the receiver first (`emit_inherent_call`).
+    fn emit_inherent_call(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        def_id: Int,
+        receiver: HirExpr,
+        args: Vec<HirExpr>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        // An associated function has no receiver.
+        if self.selfless.at(def_id) {
+            let mname = self.shown_method(def_id)
+            self.error(
+                "E0014",
+                "`${mname}` is an associated function with no `self` receiver; call it as `Type::${mname}(…)`",
+                span,
+            )
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        let sig = match self.sigs.at(def_id) {
+            Some(s) => s
+            None => return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        // `params[0]` is `self`.
+        let expected_args = if sig.params.len() > 0 { sig.params.len() - 1 } else { 0 }
+        if args.len() != expected_args {
+            let mname = self.shown_method(def_id)
+            self.error(
+                "E0016",
+                "`${mname}` takes ${expected_args} argument(s) but ${args.len()} were supplied",
+                span,
+            )
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        // A generic impl's parameters, fresh, recovered from the receiver
+        // and the arguments.
+        let mut type_args: Vec<Ty> = Vec::new()
+        for _ in 0..sig.generics { type_args.push(fcx.icx.fresh()) }
+        let self_param = subst(sig.params.at(0), type_args)
+        // The receiver must fit the impl's self type exactly.
+        if !fcx.icx.unify(receiver.ty, self_param) {
+            let mname = self.shown_method(def_id)
+            self.error(
+                "E0014",
+                "method `${mname}` does not apply to receiver of type `${self.show(receiver.ty, fcx)}`",
+                span,
+            )
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        for k in 0..args.len() {
+            let arg = args.at(k)
+            let expected = subst(sig.params.at(k + 1), type_args)
+            if !fcx.icx.unify(arg.ty, expected) {
+                self.error(
+                    "E0010",
+                    "argument has type `${self.show(arg.ty, fcx)}` but `${self.show(expected, fcx)}` was expected",
+                    arg.span,
+                )
+            }
+        }
+        let ret = subst(sig.ret, type_args)
+        let mut call_args: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+        call_args.push(receiver)
+        for a in args.iter() { call_args.push(a) }
+        HirExpr { kind: EkCall(CalleeDef(def_id), type_args, call_args), ty: ret, span: span }
+    }
+
+    /// An associated function's call, `Type::f(args)`, with no receiver
+    /// (`emit_assoc_call`).
+    pub fn emit_assoc_call(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        def_id: Int,
+        args: Vec<HirExpr>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let sig = match self.sigs.at(def_id) {
+            Some(s) => s
+            None => return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        if args.len() != sig.params.len() {
+            let fname = self.name_of(def_id)
+            self.error(
+                "E0016",
+                "`${fname}` takes ${sig.params.len()} argument(s) but ${args.len()} were supplied",
+                span,
+            )
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        let mut type_args: Vec<Ty> = Vec::new()
+        for _ in 0..sig.generics { type_args.push(fcx.icx.fresh()) }
+        for k in 0..args.len() {
+            let arg = args.at(k)
+            let expected = subst(sig.params.at(k), type_args)
+            if !fcx.icx.unify(arg.ty, expected) {
+                self.error(
+                    "E0010",
+                    "argument has type `${self.show(arg.ty, fcx)}` but `${self.show(expected, fcx)}` was expected",
+                    arg.span,
+                )
+            }
+        }
+        let ret = subst(sig.ret, type_args)
+        HirExpr { kind: EkCall(CalleeDef(def_id), type_args, args), ty: ret, span: span }
+    }
+
+    /// A trait method's call, the only maker of `TraitCall`; `dispatch`
+    /// says where `Self` comes from (`emit_trait_call`).
+    pub fn emit_trait_call(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        trait_id: Int,
+        method_idx: Int,
+        dispatch: TraitCallSelf,
+        args: Vec<HirExpr>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let mut found: Option<TraitMethod> = None
+        for t in self.traits.iter() {
+            if t.def_id == trait_id {
+                if method_idx >= 0 && method_idx < t.methods.len() {
+                    found = Some(t.methods.at(method_idx))
+                }
+                break
+            }
+        }
+        let tm = match found {
+            Some(m) => m
+            None => return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        // The receiver's presence must agree with what the trait declares.
+        let (self_ty, receiver) = match dispatch {
+            TraitCallSelfReceiver(recv, recv_ast) => {
+                if !tm.has_self {
+                    self.error(
+                        "E0014",
+                        "`${tm.name}` is an associated function with no `self` receiver; call it as `Type::${tm.name}(…)`",
+                        span,
+                    )
+                    return error_expr(span)
+                }
+                // The mutable-receiver rule, on the trait's own flag, before
+                // the arity and the arguments, without returning.
+                if tm.mut_self {
+                    self.require_mutable_place(fcx, recv_ast, span, MutTargetReceiver(tm.name))
+                }
+                let r: Option<HirExpr> = Some(recv)
+                (fcx.icx.apply(recv.ty), r)
+            }
+            TraitCallSelfQualifier(ty) => {
+                if tm.has_self {
+                    self.error(
+                        "E0014",
+                        "`${tm.name}` is a method with a `self` receiver; call it on a value as `value.${tm.name}(…)`",
+                        span,
+                    )
+                    return error_expr(span)
+                }
+                let r: Option<HirExpr> = None
+                (ty, r)
+            }
+        }
+        // `Self` is `Param(0)`, the method's own generics `Param(1..)`,
+        // fresh.
+        let mut type_args: Vec<Ty> = Vec::new()
+        for _ in 0..tm.generics { type_args.push(fcx.icx.fresh()) }
+        let mut sub: Vec<Ty> = Vec::new()
+        sub.push(self_ty)
+        for t in type_args.iter() { sub.push(t) }
+        if args.len() != tm.params.len() {
+            self.error(
+                "E0016",
+                "`${tm.name}` takes ${tm.params.len()} argument(s) but ${args.len()} were supplied",
+                span,
+            )
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        for k in 0..args.len() {
+            let arg = args.at(k)
+            // A parameter may be `Self::Item`.
+            let expected = self.instantiate(tm.params.at(k), sub, fcx.icx, arg.span)
+            if !fcx.icx.unify(arg.ty, expected) {
+                self.error(
+                    "E0010",
+                    "argument has type `${self.show(arg.ty, fcx)}` but `${self.show(expected, fcx)}` was expected",
+                    arg.span,
+                )
+            }
+        }
+        // Normalization seam: the call's return type.
+        let ret = self.instantiate(tm.ret, sub, fcx.icx, span)
+        HirExpr {
+            kind: EkTraitCall(trait_id, method_idx, self_ty, type_args, receiver, args),
+            ty: ret,
+            span: span,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// When `recv_ty` has a trait's `fmt(self) -> String` in scope, the call
+    /// that makes `value`'s string, for interpolation; `value_ast` is
+    /// `value` as written (`try_display`).
+    pub fn try_display(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        value: HirExpr,
+        value_ast: Spanned<Expr>,
+        recv_ty: Ty,
+    ) -> Option<HirExpr> {
+        let (trait_id, method_idx) = match self.resolve_method_on(recv_ty, fcx, "fmt") {
+            MethodResTrait(t, i) => (t, i)
+            _ => return None
+        }
+        // No other argument, and a `String`.
+        let mut found: Option<TraitMethod> = None
+        for t in self.traits.iter() {
+            if t.def_id == trait_id {
+                if method_idx < t.methods.len() { found = Some(t.methods.at(method_idx)) }
+                break
+            }
+        }
+        let tm = found?
+        if !tm.params.is_empty() || !ty_eq(tm.ret, TyString) { return None }
+        let span = value.span
+        Some(
+            self.emit_trait_call(
+                fcx,
+                trait_id,
+                method_idx,
+                TraitCallSelfReceiver(value, value_ast),
+                Vec::new(),
+                span,
+            ),
+        )
+    }
+
+    /// A method as a diagnostic names it: an array impl's by its self type
+    /// in the impl's names, a generic named type's by its head, any other as
+    /// the resolver names it (`shown_method`).
+    pub fn shown_method(self, def_id: Int) -> String {
+        let raw = self.name_of(def_id)
+        let mut owner = -1
+        for k in 0..self.impls.len() {
+            let mut has = false
+            for (_, d) in self.impls.at(k).methods.iter() { if d == def_id { has = true } }
+            if has {
+                owner = k
+                break
+            }
+        }
+        let dot = last_dot(raw)
+        if owner < 0 || dot < 0 { return raw }
+        let method = raw.byte_slice(dot + 1, raw.byte_len())
+        let imp = self.impls.at(owner)
+        if head_eq(imp.self_head, TyHeadArray) {
+            let names = if owner < self.impl_param_names.len() {
+                self.impl_param_names.at(owner)
+            } else {
+                Vec::new()
+            }
+            let ty = display_ty_named(imp.self_ty, self.defs, names)
+            return "${ty}::${method}"
+        }
+        if imp.generics > 0 {
+            let ty = display_ty(imp.self_ty, self.defs)
+            let stem = match ty.index_of("<") {
+                Some(at) => ty.byte_slice(0, at)
+                None => ty
+            }
+            return "${stem}::${method}"
+        }
+        raw
+    }
+}
+
+// The byte index of the last `.` of `s`, or -1 (`rsplit_once('.')`).
+fn last_dot(s: String) -> Int {
+    let mut k = s.byte_len()
+    while k > 0 {
+        k -= 1
+        if s.byte_at(k) == 46 { return k }
+    }
+    -1
+}
+
+// A tuple index's value, `name` all decimal digits, or -1 when it is not
+// one (`str::parse::<usize>`); a value past every tuple's length is as
+// good as none.
+fn parse_index(name: String) -> Int {
+    let n = name.byte_len()
+    if n == 0 { return -1 }
+    let mut v = 0
+    for k in 0..n {
+        let b = name.byte_at(k)
+        if b < 48 || b > 57 { return -1 }
+        // Past any tuple's length: keep it from overflowing.
+        if v > 100000000 { v = 100000000 } else { v = v * 10 + (b - 48) }
+    }
+    v
+}
diff --git a/selfhost/src/typeck_place.nova b/selfhost/src/typeck_place.nova
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..9dfb8b8d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/selfhost/src/typeck_place.nova
@@ -0,0 +1,403 @@
+// The type checker's assignments and places: a port of check.rs's
+// `check_assign`, `place_root`, `require_mutable_place`,
+// `check_index_set`, `compound_value` and `check_field_set`, with
+// `MutTarget` (`immutable_message`, `not_a_place_message`), `PlaceRoot`,
+// and the free `assign_binop`, `local_expr`, `let_expr` and `with_binds`,
+// function by function and with the same names (spec
+// docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-phase-5-3-the-type-checker-and-hir-design.md
+// §4.2, ADR 0056). typeck_body.nova gives the idioms; fixes.nova holds
+// `mutable_fix` and `immutable_note`.
+//
+// The three ways to mutate through a place (`a[i] = v`, `r.f = v`, a call
+// of a method declaring `mut self`) share `require_mutable_place`, which
+// walks the place as written, its AST, to the binding at its root.
+
+import ast
+import diagnostic
+import fixes
+import hir
+import infer
+import resolver
+import token
+import typeck
+import typeck_body
+import typeck_expr
+import typeck_method
+
+/// What `require_mutable_place` is asked to mutate (`MutTarget`): an
+/// element, a field, or the receiver of the method its name names.
+pub type MutTarget = | MutTargetElement | MutTargetField | MutTargetReceiver(String)
+
+/// The binding at a place's root (`PlaceRoot`): a mutable local, an
+/// immutable one (its name and its declaration's span), or none.
+pub type PlaceRoot = | PlaceRootMutable | PlaceRootImmutableLocal(String, Span) | PlaceRootNotAPlace
+
+/// The message when the place's root is the immutable local `name`
+/// (`MutTarget::immutable_message`).
+pub fn immutable_message(what: MutTarget, name: String) -> String {
+    match what {
+        MutTargetElement => "cannot assign to an element of immutable `${name}`"
+        MutTargetField => "cannot assign to a field of immutable `${name}`"
+        MutTargetReceiver(m) => "`${m}` mutates its receiver, but `${name}` is immutable"
+    }
+}
+
+/// The message when the place has no assignable root
+/// (`MutTarget::not_a_place_message`).
+pub fn not_a_place_message(what: MutTarget) -> String {
+    match what {
+        MutTargetElement => "cannot assign to an element of a temporary or non-assignable value"
+        MutTargetField => "cannot assign to a field of a temporary or non-assignable value"
+        MutTargetReceiver(m) => "`${m}` mutates its receiver, which cannot be a temporary"
+    }
+}
+
+impl Checker {
+    /// `lhs = rhs` and `lhs op= rhs` (`check_assign`).
+    pub fn check_assign(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        op: AssignOp,
+        lhs: Spanned<Expr>,
+        rhs: Spanned<Expr>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let path = match lhs.value {
+            // `arr[i] = v`.
+            ExprIndex(target, index) => return self.check_index_set(
+                fcx,
+                op,
+                target,
+                index,
+                rhs,
+                span,
+            )
+            // `rec.field = v`.
+            ExprField(target, field) => return self.check_field_set(
+                fcx,
+                op,
+                target,
+                field,
+                rhs,
+                span,
+            )
+            ExprPath(p) => p
+            _ => {
+                // A target with no assignable place: a call's result, a
+                // literal, a parenthesised expression.
+                self.unsupported(
+                    lhs.span,
+                    "assignments to anything but a local variable, array element, or record field",
+                )
+                return error_expr(span)
+            }
+        }
+        if path.segments.len() != 1 {
+            self.unsupported(lhs.span, "assignment to paths")
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        let name = path.segments.at(0).value
+        let local = fcx.lookup(name)
+        if local < 0 {
+            self.error("E0001", "cannot find `${name}` in this scope", lhs.span)
+            let nearby = fcx.visible_locals()
+            self.push_fix(change_to(self.cur_file, path.segments.at(0), nearby.to_array()))
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        let info = fcx.locals.at(local)
+        let info_ty = info.ty
+        let info_span = info.span
+        if !info.is_mut {
+            self.error("E0060", "cannot assign to immutable variable `${name}`", span)
+            // Where a fix is offered, it says what the note would.
+            match self.mutable_fix(name, info_span) {
+                Some(fix) => self.push_fix(Some(fix))
+                None => {
+                    let note = self.immutable_note(name, info_span, "assignment")
+                    let mut d = self.diagnostics.last()
+                    d.notes.push(note)
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        let value = self.check_expr(fcx, rhs)
+        // `x += e` is `x = x + e`.
+        let final_value = match assign_binop(op) {
+            None => value
+            Some(bin) => {
+                let lhs_read = HirExpr { kind: EkLocal(local), ty: info_ty, span: lhs.span }
+                let ty = self.binary_result_ty(fcx, bin, lhs_read, value, span)
+                HirExpr { kind: EkBinary(bin, lhs_read, value), ty: ty, span: span }
+            }
+        }
+        if !fcx.icx.unify(final_value.ty, info_ty) {
+            self.error(
+                "E0010",
+                "cannot assign `${self.show(final_value.ty, fcx)}` to `${name}` which has type `${self.show(info_ty, fcx)}`",
+                span,
+            )
+        }
+        HirExpr { kind: EkAssign(local, final_value), ty: TyUnit, span: span }
+    }
+
+    /// The binding at the root of a place, through its element and field
+    /// projections (`place_root`).
+    pub fn place_root(self, fcx: FnCtx, expr: Spanned<Expr>) -> PlaceRoot {
+        match expr.value {
+            ExprPath(p) => {
+                if p.segments.len() != 1 { return PlaceRootNotAPlace }
+                let l = fcx.lookup(p.segments.at(0).value)
+                // A constant, a path of more segments or an unknown name is
+                // no mutable place.
+                if l < 0 { return PlaceRootNotAPlace }
+                let local = fcx.locals.at(l)
+                if local.is_mut {
+                    PlaceRootMutable
+                } else {
+                    PlaceRootImmutableLocal(p.segments.at(0).value, local.span)
+                }
+            }
+            ExprIndex(target, _) => self.place_root(fcx, target)
+            ExprField(target, _) => self.place_root(fcx, target)
+            // A call's result, a literal, a block: a temporary.
+            _ => PlaceRootNotAPlace
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// E0060 unless `target`'s storage is reachable through a mutable
+    /// binding, `what` naming what is mutated (`require_mutable_place`).
+    pub fn require_mutable_place(
+        mut self,
+        fcx: FnCtx,
+        target: Spanned<Expr>,
+        span: Span,
+        what: MutTarget,
+    ) {
+        match self.place_root(fcx, target) {
+            PlaceRootMutable => ()
+            PlaceRootImmutableLocal(name, decl) => {
+                self.error("E0060", immutable_message(what, name), span)
+                // Where a fix is offered, it says what the note would.
+                match self.mutable_fix(name, decl) {
+                    Some(fix) => {
+                        self.push_fix(Some(fix))
+                        return
+                    }
+                    None => ()
+                }
+                // A receiver's mutability is declared in the signature, so
+                // a `self` root needs other advice.
+                let note = if name == "self" {
+                    "declare the enclosing method's receiver as `mut self` to allow mutation"
+                } else {
+                    self.immutable_note(name, decl, "mutation")
+                }
+                let mut d = self.diagnostics.last()
+                d.notes.push(note)
+            }
+            PlaceRootNotAPlace => self.error("E0060", not_a_place_message(what), span)
+        }
+    }
+
+    // `arr[index] = value`: `rhs` is checked on every early return
+    // (`check_index_set`).
+    fn check_index_set(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        op: AssignOp,
+        target: Spanned<Expr>,
+        index: Spanned<Expr>,
+        rhs: Spanned<Expr>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        // The whole index and field chain to its root local.
+        self.require_mutable_place(fcx, target, span, MutTargetElement)
+        let arr = self.check_expr(fcx, target)
+        let idx = self.check_expr(fcx, index)
+        self.expect_ty(fcx, idx, TyInt, "an array index")
+        let elem_ty = fcx.icx.fresh()
+        if !fcx.icx.unify(arr.ty, TyArray(elem_ty)) {
+            self.error(
+                "E0014",
+                "cannot index-assign a value of type `${self.show(arr.ty, fcx)}`",
+                target.span,
+            )
+            let _ = self.check_expr(fcx, rhs)
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        // `a[i] op= e`: the array and the index into unscoped locals,
+        // evaluated once, then `a[k] = a[k] op e` stores.
+        let bin = assign_binop(op)
+        let mut place = -1
+        let mut key = -1
+        let mut arr_ty = TyError
+        match bin {
+            Some(_) => {
+                arr_ty = fcx.icx.apply(arr.ty)
+                place = fcx.new_local_unscoped("__place", arr_ty, false, span)
+                key = fcx.new_local_unscoped("__index", TyInt, false, span)
+            }
+            None => ()
+        }
+        let mut binds: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+        let (arr, idx) = match bin {
+            None => (arr, idx)
+            Some(_) => {
+                binds.push(let_expr(place, arr, span))
+                binds.push(let_expr(key, idx, span))
+                (local_expr(place, arr_ty, target.span), local_expr(key, TyInt, index.span))
+            }
+        }
+        let value = self.check_expr(fcx, rhs)
+        let value = match bin {
+            None => value
+            Some(b) => {
+                let old = HirExpr {
+                    kind: EkIndex(
+                        local_expr(place, arr_ty, target.span),
+                        local_expr(key, TyInt, index.span),
+                    ),
+                    ty: elem_ty,
+                    span: target.span.merge(index.span),
+                }
+                self.compound_value(fcx, b, old, value, span)
+            }
+        }
+        if !fcx.icx.unify(value.ty, elem_ty) {
+            self.error(
+                "E0010",
+                "array element has type `${self.show(elem_ty, fcx)}` but `${self.show(value.ty, fcx)}` was assigned",
+                rhs.span,
+            )
+        }
+        let set = HirExpr { kind: EkIndexSet(arr, idx, value), ty: TyUnit, span: span }
+        with_binds(binds, set, span)
+    }
+
+    // `old op value`, what a compound assignment stores, by a binary
+    // expression's rules (`compound_value`).
+    fn compound_value(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        bin: HirBinOp,
+        old: HirExpr,
+        value: HirExpr,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let ty = self.binary_result_ty(fcx, bin, old, value, span)
+        HirExpr { kind: EkBinary(bin, old, value), ty: ty, span: span }
+    }
+
+    // `target.field = value`: `rhs` is checked on every early return
+    // (`check_field_set`).
+    fn check_field_set(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        op: AssignOp,
+        target: Spanned<Expr>,
+        field: Spanned<String>,
+        rhs: Spanned<Expr>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        // The whole field and index chain to its root local.
+        self.require_mutable_place(fcx, target, span, MutTargetField)
+        let rec = self.check_expr(fcx, target)
+        let recv_ty = fcx.icx.apply(rec.ty)
+        // A broken receiver reported its own error.
+        match recv_ty {
+            TyError => {
+                let _ = self.check_expr(fcx, rhs)
+                return error_expr(span)
+            }
+            _ => ()
+        }
+        // The same lookup reads use, so reads and writes agree on layout.
+        let (index, field_ty) = match self.record_field_index_and_ty(
+            fcx,
+            recv_ty,
+            field.value,
+            span,
+        ) {
+            Some(found) => found
+            None => {
+                if self.tuple_index_on_unknown(fcx, recv_ty, field) {
+                    let _ = self.check_expr(fcx, rhs)
+                    return error_expr(span)
+                }
+                self.error("E0014", self.no_field_message(fcx, recv_ty, field.value), field.span)
+                let fix = self.field_fix(recv_ty, field)
+                self.push_fix(fix)
+                let _ = self.check_expr(fcx, rhs)
+                return error_expr(span)
+            }
+        }
+        // `r.f op= e`: the receiver into an unscoped local, evaluated once,
+        // then `t.f = t.f op e` stores.
+        let bin = assign_binop(op)
+        let mut place = -1
+        let mut binds: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+        let rec = match bin {
+            None => rec
+            Some(_) => {
+                place = fcx.new_local_unscoped("__place", recv_ty, false, span)
+                binds.push(let_expr(place, rec, span))
+                local_expr(place, recv_ty, target.span)
+            }
+        }
+        let value = self.check_expr(fcx, rhs)
+        let value = match bin {
+            None => value
+            Some(b) => {
+                let old = HirExpr {
+                    kind: EkFieldGet(local_expr(place, recv_ty, target.span), index),
+                    ty: field_ty,
+                    span: target.span.merge(field.span),
+                }
+                self.compound_value(fcx, b, old, value, span)
+            }
+        }
+        if !fcx.icx.unify(value.ty, field_ty) {
+            self.error(
+                "E0010",
+                "field `${field.value}` has type `${self.show(field_ty, fcx)}` but `${self.show(value.ty, fcx)}` was assigned",
+                rhs.span,
+            )
+        }
+        let set = HirExpr { kind: EkFieldSet(rec, index, value), ty: TyUnit, span: span }
+        with_binds(binds, set, span)
+    }
+}
+
+/// A compound assignment's operator, `None` for `=` (`assign_binop`).
+pub fn assign_binop(op: AssignOp) -> Option<HirBinOp> {
+    match op {
+        AssignOpAssign => None
+        AssignOpAddAssign => Some(OpAdd)
+        AssignOpSubAssign => Some(OpSub)
+        AssignOpMulAssign => Some(OpMul)
+        AssignOpDivAssign => Some(OpDiv)
+        AssignOpRemAssign => Some(OpRem)
+        AssignOpBitOrAssign => Some(OpBitOr)
+        AssignOpBitAndAssign => Some(OpBitAnd)
+        AssignOpBitXorAssign => Some(OpBitXor)
+        AssignOpShlAssign => Some(OpShl)
+        AssignOpShrAssign => Some(OpShr)
+    }
+}
+
+/// A read of `local` (`local_expr`).
+pub fn local_expr(local: Int, ty: Ty, span: Span) -> HirExpr {
+    HirExpr { kind: EkLocal(local), ty: ty, span: span }
+}
+
+/// `let local = init`, of type `()` (`let_expr`).
+pub fn let_expr(local: Int, init: HirExpr, span: Span) -> HirExpr {
+    HirExpr { kind: EkLet(local, init), ty: TyUnit, span: span }
+}
+
+/// `expr` after `binds`, in one block of type `()`; `expr` alone when
+/// there are none (`with_binds`).
+pub fn with_binds(mut binds: Vec<HirExpr>, expr: HirExpr, span: Span) -> HirExpr {
+    if binds.is_empty() { return expr }
+    binds.push(expr)
+    HirExpr { kind: EkBlock(binds, None), ty: TyUnit, span: span }
+}
````

````diff
index 8f410d87..25233c07 100644
--- a/crates/nova-cli/tests/selfhost.rs
+++ b/crates/nova-cli/tests/selfhost.rs
@@ -4888,14 +4888,15 @@ fn n_bodies_on(

new file mode 100644
index 00000000..0c8cf14e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/selfhost/src/typeck_pattern_tests.nova
@@ -0,0 +1,394 @@
+// N's own tests of `match`, patterns, usefulness and `for` (5.3b part 4).
+// The usefulness tests mirror crates/nova-typeck/src/usefulness.rs's,
+// which stay Rust's too; the others check a program, each expected value
+// what S0's `nova check` gives for the same source. The sources need no
+// std (typeck_body_tests.nova's `check_bodies_of`). The differential
+// compares every other input.
+//
+// They live in `src/`, imported by `main.nova`, for the reason
+// lexer_tests.nova gives.
+
+import diagnostic
+import hir
+import token
+import typeck
+import typeck_body
+import typeck_body_tests
+import typeck_pattern
+import usefulness
+
+// --- usefulness.rs's tests ---
+
+// A constructor with no argument.
+fn ctor(c: Ctor) -> UPat { UpCtor(c, Vec::new()) }
+
+// The witnesses of a wildcard against `rows`, a column of type `ty`, each
+// its one pattern.
+fn witnesses(cx: MatchCx, rows: Vec<UPat>, ty: Ty) -> Vec<UPat> {
+    let mut matrix: Vec<Vec<UPat>> = Vec::new()
+    for r in rows.iter() { matrix.push(one(r)) }
+    let mut out: Vec<UPat> = Vec::new()
+    for w in cx.usefulness(matrix, one(UpWild), col(ty)).iter() { out.push(w.at(0)) }
+    out
+}
+
+fn col(ty: Ty) -> Vec<Ty> {
+    let mut tys: Vec<Ty> = Vec::new()
+    tys.push(ty)
+    tys
+}
+
+// Whether `q` is useful against the rows `prior`.
+fn useful(cx: MatchCx, prior: Vec<UPat>, q: UPat, ty: Ty) -> Bool {
+    let mut matrix: Vec<Vec<UPat>> = Vec::new()
+    for r in prior.iter() { matrix.push(one(r)) }
+    !cx.usefulness(matrix, one(q), col(ty)).is_empty()
+}
+
+fn pats(ps: [UPat]) -> Vec<UPat> { Vec::from_array(ps) }
+
+fn no_sums() -> MatchCx { new_match_cx(Vec::new()) }
+
+const OPT: Int = 1
+
+const RES: Int = 2
+
+// `Opt<T> = Some(T) | None` and `Res<T, E> = Ok(T) | Err(E)`.
+fn sums() -> MatchCx {
+    let mut out: Vec<SumType> = Vec::new()
+    let mut opt: Vec<HirVariant> = Vec::new()
+    opt.push(HirVariant { name: "Some", fields: Vec::from_array([TyParam(0)]) })
+    opt.push(HirVariant { name: "None", fields: Vec::new() })
+    out.push(SumType { def_id: OPT, name: "Opt", generics: 1, variants: opt })
+    let mut res: Vec<HirVariant> = Vec::new()
+    res.push(HirVariant { name: "Ok", fields: Vec::from_array([TyParam(0)]) })
+    res.push(HirVariant { name: "Err", fields: Vec::from_array([TyParam(1)]) })
+    out.push(SumType { def_id: RES, name: "Res", generics: 2, variants: res })
+    new_match_cx(out)
+}
+
+fn opt(t: Ty) -> Ty { TySum(OPT, Vec::from_array([t])) }
+
+fn res(t: Ty, e: Ty) -> Ty { TySum(RES, Vec::from_array([t, e])) }
+
+fn some(p: UPat) -> UPat { UpCtor(CtorVariant(OPT, 0), one(p)) }
+
+fn none() -> UPat { UpCtor(CtorVariant(OPT, 1), Vec::new()) }
+
+fn ok(p: UPat) -> UPat { UpCtor(CtorVariant(RES, 0), one(p)) }
+
+fn err(p: UPat) -> UPat { UpCtor(CtorVariant(RES, 1), one(p)) }
+
+fn tuple(ps: [UPat]) -> UPat { UpCtor(CtorTuple(ps.len()), Vec::from_array(ps)) }
+
+// Whether `p` is constructor `c` (its arguments not looked at).
+fn is_ctor(p: UPat, c: Ctor) -> Bool {
+    match p {
+        UpCtor(x, _) => ctor_eq(x, c)
+        _ => false
+    }
+}
+
+// `p`'s `i`-th argument.
+fn arg(p: UPat, i: Int) -> UPat {
+    match p {
+        UpCtor(_, args) => args.at(i)
+        _ => UpWild
+    }
+}
+
+fn is_wild(p: UPat) -> Bool {
+    match p {
+        UpWild => true
+        _ => false
+    }
+}
+
+@test
+fn bool_true_and_false_is_exhaustive() {
+    let w = witnesses(no_sums(), pats([ctor(CtorBool(true)), ctor(CtorBool(false))]), TyBool)
+    assert(w.is_empty(), "exhaustive")
+}
+
+@test
+fn bool_missing_false_yields_false_witness() {
+    let w = witnesses(no_sums(), pats([ctor(CtorBool(true))]), TyBool)
+    assert(w.len() == 1 && is_ctor(w.at(0), CtorBool(false)), "`false`")
+}
+
+@test
+fn int_literals_need_a_wildcard() {
+    let w = witnesses(no_sums(), pats([ctor(CtorInt(0)), ctor(CtorInt(1))]), TyInt)
+    assert(w.len() == 1 && is_wild(w.at(0)), "`_`")
+}
+
+@test
+fn int_with_wildcard_is_exhaustive() {
+    assert(witnesses(no_sums(), pats([ctor(CtorInt(0)), UpWild]), TyInt).is_empty(), "exhaustive")
+}
+
+@test
+fn arm_covered_by_earlier_wildcard_is_not_useful() {
+    assert(!useful(no_sums(), pats([UpWild]), ctor(CtorInt(1)), TyInt), "unreachable")
+}
+
+@test
+fn distinct_literal_is_useful() {
+    assert(useful(no_sums(), pats([ctor(CtorInt(0))]), ctor(CtorInt(1)), TyInt), "reachable")
+}
+
+@test
+fn a_nested_witness_names_the_inner_variant() {
+    let w = witnesses(sums(), pats([some(ok(UpWild)), none()]), opt(res(TyInt, TyString)))
+    assert(w.len() == 1, "one witness")
+    assert(is_ctor(w.at(0), CtorVariant(OPT, 0)), "`Some(…)`")
+    assert(is_ctor(arg(w.at(0), 0), CtorVariant(RES, 1)), "`Some(Err(_))`")
+}
+
+@test
+fn a_nested_arm_an_earlier_one_covers_is_not_useful() {
+    let ty = opt(opt(TyInt))
+    assert(!useful(sums(), pats([some(UpWild)]), some(some(ctor(CtorInt(1)))), ty), "covered")
+    // First match wins: the more specific arm first leaves the general one
+    // useful.
+    assert(useful(sums(), pats([some(some(ctor(CtorInt(1))))]), some(UpWild), ty), "useful")
+}
+
+@test
+fn an_or_pattern_row_covers_every_alternative() {
+    let ty = opt(res(TyInt, TyInt))
+    let rows = pats([some(UpOr(pats([ok(UpWild), err(UpWild)]))), none()])
+    assert(witnesses(sums(), rows, ty).is_empty(), "exhaustive")
+    // An or-pattern as the candidate row is useful when one alternative is.
+    let prior = pats([some(ok(UpWild))])
+    assert(useful(sums(), prior, UpOr(pats([some(ok(UpWild)), none()])), ty), "useful")
+    assert(!useful(sums(), prior, UpOr(pats([some(ok(ctor(CtorInt(3))))])), ty), "not useful")
+}
+
+@test
+fn a_tuple_of_sums_needs_every_combination() {
+    let ty = TyTuple(Vec::from_array([opt(TyInt), TyBool]))
+    let mut rows = pats([tuple([some(UpWild), UpWild]), tuple([none(), ctor(CtorBool(true))])])
+    let w = witnesses(sums(), rows, ty)
+    assert(w.len() == 1 && is_ctor(w.at(0), CtorTuple(2)), "one tuple witness")
+    assert(is_ctor(arg(w.at(0), 0), CtorVariant(OPT, 1)), "`(None, …)`")
+    assert(is_ctor(arg(w.at(0), 1), CtorBool(false)), "`(None, false)`")
+    rows.push(tuple([UpWild, ctor(CtorBool(false))]))
+    assert(witnesses(sums(), rows, ty).is_empty(), "exhaustive")
+}
+
+@test
+fn a_tuple_is_one_constructor_even_when_its_type_is_unknown() {
+    assert(witnesses(sums(), pats([tuple([UpWild, UpWild])]), TyError).is_empty(), "exhaustive")
+}
+
+@test
+fn literals_and_ranges_inside_a_variant_need_a_catch_all() {
+    let ty = opt(TyChar)
+    let mut rows = pats([some(ctor(CtorRange(97, 122))), some(ctor(CtorChar('_'))), none()])
+    let w = witnesses(sums(), rows, ty)
+    assert(w.len() == 1 && is_ctor(w.at(0), CtorVariant(OPT, 0)), "`Some(…)`")
+    assert(is_wild(arg(w.at(0), 0)), "`Some(_)`")
+    rows.push(some(UpWild))
+    assert(witnesses(sums(), rows, ty).is_empty(), "exhaustive")
+}
+
+@test
+fn ranges_are_not_split() {
+    // The same range again is not useful; one inside it still is.
+    let prior = pats([ctor(CtorRange(1, 10))])
+    assert(!useful(no_sums(), prior, ctor(CtorRange(1, 10)), TyInt), "the same range")
+    assert(useful(no_sums(), prior, ctor(CtorRange(2, 3)), TyInt), "a range inside")
+    assert(useful(no_sums(), prior, ctor(CtorInt(5)), TyInt), "a literal inside")
+    // A range covering every `Int` still needs a catch-all.
+    let all = pats([ctor(CtorRange(-9223372036854775807 - 1, 9223372036854775807))])
+    assert(useful(no_sums(), all, UpWild, TyInt), "a catch-all")
+}
+
+@test
+fn a_generic_sum_at_depth_takes_its_arguments() {
+    // `Opt<Opt<Bool>>`: `Some(Some(true))`, `Some(Some(false))`, `None`
+    // leave `Some(None)`.
+    let rows = pats([some(some(ctor(CtorBool(true)))), some(some(ctor(CtorBool(false)))), none()])
+    let w = witnesses(sums(), rows, opt(opt(TyBool)))
+    assert(w.len() == 1 && is_ctor(w.at(0), CtorVariant(OPT, 0)), "`Some(…)`")
+    assert(is_ctor(arg(w.at(0), 0), CtorVariant(OPT, 1)), "`Some(None)`")
+}
+
+@test
+fn a_witness_names_a_value_the_literals_miss_where_e0022_asks() {
+    // `0` past a range from 1, `'a'` beside `'b'`, `"a"` past `""`.
+    let cx = no_sums().naming_values()
+    let w = witnesses(cx, pats([ctor(CtorRange(-5, -1)), ctor(CtorInt(0))]), TyInt)
+    assert(w.len() == 1 && is_ctor(w.at(0), CtorInt(1)), "`1`")
+    let w = witnesses(cx, pats([ctor(CtorChar('b'))]), TyChar)
+    assert(w.len() == 1 && is_ctor(w.at(0), CtorChar('a')), "`'a'`")
+    let w = witnesses(cx, pats([ctor(CtorStr(""))]), TyString)
+    assert(w.len() == 1 && is_ctor(w.at(0), CtorStr("a")), "`\"a\"`")
+}
+
+// --- Patterns and `match` in a program ---
+
+// Each diagnostic's code, message and primary label, its notes, and each
+// fix's title and edits, one a line.
+fn report(c: Checker) -> String {
+    let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new()
+    for d in c.diagnostics.iter() {
+        let l = d.labels.at(0)
+        out.push("${d.code} ${d.message} ${l.span.start}..${l.span.end} ${l.message}")
+        for n in d.notes.iter() { out.push("  note: ${n}") }
+        for f in d.fixes.iter() {
+            out.push("  fix: ${f.title}")
+            for e in f.edits.iter() { out.push("    ${e.span.start}..${e.span.end} `${e.text}`") }
+        }
+    }
+    "\n".join(out.to_array())
+}
+
+// "" when `c`'s report is `want`, one entry a line, else what it is.
+fn mismatch(c: Checker, want: [String]) -> String {
+    let got = report(c)
+    if got == "\n".join(want) { "" } else { "got: ${" | ".join(got.split("\n"))}" }
+}
+
+@test
+fn a_missing_nested_variant_is_the_witness() {
+    let c = check_bodies_of(
+        "type S = | A | B(Int) | C(Bool)\nfn f(s: S) -> Int {\n    match s {\n        A => 0\n        B(_) => 1\n        C(true) => 2\n    }\n}\n",
+    )
+    let m = mismatch(
+        c,
+        [
+            "E0020 non-exhaustive match: pattern `C(false)` not covered 56..125 here",
+            "  note: add the missing arms or a `_ => ...` catch-all",
+        ],
+    )
+    assert(m == "", m)
+}
+
+@test
+fn an_unreachable_arm_has_its_line_removed() {
+    let c = check_bodies_of(
+        "fn f(x: Int) -> Int {\n    match x {\n        _ => 0\n        1 => 1\n    }\n}\n",
+    )
+    let m = mismatch(
+        c,
+        [
+            "E0021 unreachable match arm 59..60 this arm is never reached",
+            "  note: an earlier arm already matches every value this one would",
+            "  fix: remove the unreachable arm",
+            "    51..66 ``",
+        ],
+    )
+    assert(m == "", m)
+}
+
+@test
+fn a_refutable_let_and_for_name_the_values_they_miss() {
+    let c = check_bodies_of(
+        "fn f(p: (Int, Bool), q: [(Int, Bool)]) -> Int {\n    let (a, true) = p\n    for (1, true) in q { }\n    a\n}\n",
+    )
+    let note = "  note: `let` and `for` take a pattern every value matches: names, `_`, tuples of these, and a variant of a sum that has only one; use `match` for the rest"
+    let m = mismatch(
+        c,
+        [
+            "E0022 refutable pattern in `let` 56..65 `(_, false)` is not matched",
+            note,
+            "E0022 refutable pattern in a `for` loop 78..87 `(0, _)`, `(1, false)` are not matched",
+            note,
+        ],
+    )
+    assert(m == "", m)

+@test
+fn an_upper_case_binding_near_a_variant_is_e0104_with_its_fix() {
+    let c = check_bodies_of(
+        "type S = | Apple | Pear\nfn f(s: S) -> Int {\n    match s {\n        Aple => 0\n    }\n}\n",
+    )
+    let m = mismatch(
+        c,
+        [
+            "E0104 `Aple` binds a value: no variant of that name is in scope 66..70 this binding matches any value",
+            "  note: a name that starts with an upper-case letter reads as a variant; if one was meant, check its spelling or import it; to bind a value, use a lower-case name",
+            "  note: did you mean `Apple`?",
+            "  fix: change `Aple` to `Apple`",
+            "    66..70 `Apple`",
+        ],
+    )
+    assert(m == "", m)
+}
+
+@test
+fn alternatives_bind_the_same_names_and_a_range_is_not_empty() {
+    let c = check_bodies_of(
+        "type O = | Some(Int) | None\nfn f(o: O) -> Int {\n    match o {\n        Some(x) | None => 0\n    }\n}\nfn g(c: Char) -> Int {\n    match c {\n        'z'..='a' => 0\n        _ => 1\n    }\n}\n",
+    )
+    let m = mismatch(
+        c,
+        [
+            "E0100 the alternatives bind different names 80..84 `x` is missing from this alternative",
+            "  note: every alternative of an or-pattern binds the same names; the first one binds `x`",
+            "E0101 this range matches nothing 143..152 `'z'` is above `'a'`",
+        ],
+    )
+    assert(m == "", m)
+}
+
+@test
+fn a_string_column_needs_a_catch_all() {
+    let c = check_bodies_of(
+        "fn f(s: String, c: Char) -> Int {\n    match (s, c) {\n        (\"\", 'a') => 0\n        (\"a\", '\\n') => 1\n    }\n}\n",
+    )
+    let m = mismatch(
+        c,
+        [
+            "E0020 non-exhaustive match: pattern `(_, _)` not covered 38..106 here",
+            "  note: add the missing arms or a `_ => ...` catch-all",
+        ],
+    )
+    assert(m == "", m)
+}
+
+@test
+fn a_witness_prints_strings_and_chars_as_rust_does() {
+    assert(debug_str("a\"b\\\n") == "\"a\\\"b\\\\\\n\"", debug_str("a\"b\\\n"))
+    assert(debug_char('\'') == "'\\''", debug_char('\''))
+    assert(debug_char('"') == "'\"'", debug_char('"'))
+    let del = string_from_chars([char_from_int(127).unwrap()])
+    let want = "\"" + "\\" + "u{7f}é\""
+    assert(debug_str("${del}é") == want, debug_str("${del}é"))
+}
+
+// --- `for` ---
+
+// The names of `f`'s locals, in order.
+fn local_names(f: HirFunction) -> String {
+    let mut names: Vec<String> = Vec::new()
+    for l in f.locals.iter() { names.push(l.name) }
+    " ".join(names.to_array())
+}
+
+@test
+fn a_for_loop_makes_its_hidden_locals_where_s0_does() {
+    let c = check_bodies_of(
+        "type Opt<T> = | Some(T) | None\nrecord C { n: Int }\ntrait It { fn next(mut self) -> Opt<Int> }\nimpl It for C { fn next(mut self) -> Opt<Int> { None } }\nfn f(c: C) -> Int {\n    let mut t = 0\n    for x in c { t += x }\n    for i in 0..=3 { t += i }\n    t\n}\n",
+    )
+    assert(c.diagnostics.is_empty(), report(c))
+    let f = c.functions.at(0)
+    assert(f.name == "f", "the first function is `f`")
+    // An iterator's `__it`, then a range's counter and bound, its variable,
+    // and `__run` after the body.
+    let names = local_names(f)
+    assert(names == "c t __it x __i __end i __run", names)
+}
+
+@test
+fn an_array_loop_reads_each_element_by_index() {
+    let c = check_bodies_of(
+        "fn f(a: [Int]) -> Int {\n    let mut t = 0\n    for x in a { t += x }\n    t\n}\n",
+    )
+    assert(c.diagnostics.is_empty(), report(c))
+    let names = local_names(c.functions.at(0))
+    assert(names == "a t __arr __n __i x", names)
+}
````

````diff
+/// The bytes an unreachable arm's removal takes, the arm being `start` to
+/// `end` of `text`: its whole lines, when nothing else is on them but a
+/// comment after it, and a `,` after it; none when something other than
+/// a `,`, a line's end, a `}` or a comment follows it (`arm_removal`).
+pub fn arm_removal(text: String, start: Int, end: Int) -> Option<(Int, Int)> {
+    let n = text.byte_len()
+    let mut after = skip_blanks(text, end)
+    if after < n {
+        let b = text.byte_at(after)
+        let comment_here = b == 47 && after + 1 < n && text.byte_at(after + 1) == 47
+        if b == 44 {
+            after = skip_blanks(text, after + 1)
+        } else if b != 13 && b != 10 && b != 125 && !comment_here {
+            return None
+        }
+    }
+    let first = line_start(text, start)
+    let mut alone_before = true
+    for i in first..start {
+        let b = text.byte_at(i)
+        if b != 32 && b != 9 { alone_before = false }
+    }
+    let comment = after + 1 < n && text.byte_at(after) == 47 && text.byte_at(after + 1) == 47
+    let alone_after = comment
+        || after >= n
+        || text.byte_at(after) == 13
+        || text.byte_at(after) == 10
+    if alone_before && alone_after {
+        Some((first, next_line_start(text, after)))
+    } else {
+        Some((start, after))
+    }
+}
+
+// The first byte from `from` on that is not a space or a tab.
+fn skip_blanks(text: String, from: Int) -> Int {
+    let mut i = from
+    while i < text.byte_len() && (text.byte_at(i) == 32 || text.byte_at(i) == 9) { i += 1 }
+    i
+}

-                None => ()
+            for (def_id, item_index) in const_ids.iter() {
+                if (def_id >= std_def) != in_std || self.unported != "" { continue }
+                match self.check_const(def_id, item_index) {

+                    None => ()

-        self.std_closures = self.next_closure_def
+        self.std_closures = std_closures
         self.check_const_cycles(functions)
         self.warn_newline_splits()

@@ -467,9 +478,19 @@ impl Checker {
                         PatternIdent(m, n) => (n.value, m, n.span)
                         PatternWildcard => ("_", false, pattern.span)

-                            // 5.3b part 4: a destructuring `let` binds by a
-                            // pattern, which `check_pattern` checks.
-                            self.unported_at("destructuring `let` patterns (5.3b part 4)")
+                            // Destructuring: an irrefutable pattern, bound
+                            // by a one-arm `match`. `let mut` makes each of

+                            self.pats.mutable = is_mut
+                            self.pats.let_head = Some(let_head(pattern.value))

diff --git a/selfhost/src/typeck_for.nova b/selfhost/src/typeck_for.nova
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..fee93d40
--- /dev/null
+++ b/selfhost/src/typeck_for.nova
@@ -0,0 +1,438 @@
+// The type checker's `for` loops: a port of check.rs's `check_for`,
+// `check_for_iterator`, `iterator_next` and `IteratorNext`, and of
+// check/patterns.rs's `LoopBind`, `let_pattern`, `for_loop_binding` and
+// `check_for_array`, function by function and with the same names (spec
+// docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-phase-5-3-the-type-checker-and-hir-design.md
+// §4.2, ADR 0056). typeck_pattern.nova checks the patterns a loop binds;
+// typeck_body.nova gives the idioms.
+//
+// - A loop desugars to blocks, `let`s, a `while` and, over an iterator, a
+//   `match` on `next`, each node made new where S0 makes one, so that
+//   finalizing, which rewrites a node in place, meets each once.
+// - The hidden locals are made where S0 makes them, in its order, as
+//   their ids reach the dump: a range's `__run` after the body.
+
+import ast
+import fixes
+import hir
+import infer
+import token
+import typeck
+import typeck_body
+import typeck_expr
+import typeck_method
+import typeck_pattern
+
+/// The `next` a `for` loop drives, as `iterator_next` resolved it
+/// (`IteratorNext`): the trait and the method's index; the sum `next`
+/// returns, `Option` in std, read off the same trait declaration; the
+/// index of its one-field `Some` and of its empty `None`.
+record IteratorNext { trait_id: Int, method_idx: Int, option: Int, some: Int, none: Int }
+
+/// How a `for` loop binds each element (`LoopBind`): a plain local, or an
+/// irrefutable pattern.
+pub type LoopBind = | LoopBindLocal(Int) | LoopBindPattern(HirPattern)
+
+/// The pattern that binds an element, for a `match` arm
+/// (`LoopBind::into_pattern`).
+pub fn loop_bind_pattern(b: LoopBind) -> HirPattern {
+    match b {
+        LoopBindLocal(l) => PatBind(l)
+        LoopBindPattern(p) => p
+    }
+}
+
+/// The statement that binds `init`: a `let` for a plain local, and for a
+/// pattern a one-arm `match` whose arm binds the pattern's locals for the
+/// rest of the block (`LoopBind::bind`).
+pub fn loop_bind(b: LoopBind, init: HirExpr, span: Span) -> HirExpr {
+    match b {
+        LoopBindLocal(local) => HirExpr { kind: EkLet(local, init), ty: TyUnit, span: span }
+        LoopBindPattern(pattern) => let_pattern(pattern, init, span)
+    }
+}
+
+/// `let P = init` for a destructuring `P`: a `match` with one arm, whose
+/// body is `()` (`let_pattern`).
+pub fn let_pattern(pattern: HirPattern, init: HirExpr, span: Span) -> HirExpr {
+    let mut arms: Vec<HirArm> = Vec::new()
+    arms.push(
+        HirArm {
+            pattern: pattern,
+            guard: None,
+            body: HirExpr { kind: EkUnit, ty: TyUnit, span: span },
+            span: span,
+        },
+    )
+    HirExpr { kind: EkMatch(init, arms), ty: TyUnit, span: span }
+}
+
+impl Checker {
+    /// `for p in iter { body }` (`check_for`): over `lo..hi` or `lo..=hi`
+    /// a counted `while`; otherwise `check_for_iterator`.
+    pub fn check_for(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        pattern: Spanned<Pattern>,
+        iter: Spanned<Expr>,
+        body: Spanned<Block>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let (lo_ast, hi_ast, inclusive) = match iter.value {
+            ExprRange(lo, hi, inclusive) => (lo, hi, inclusive)
+            _ => return self.check_for_iterator(fcx, pattern, iter, body, span)
+        }
+        let lo = self.check_expr(fcx, lo_ast)
+        self.expect_ty(fcx, lo, TyInt, "a range bound")
+        let hi = self.check_expr(fcx, hi_ast)
+        self.expect_ty(fcx, hi, TyInt, "a range bound")
+        // Hidden counter and bound locals, unscoped so they neither collide
+        // with nor shadow a source name; the counter is apart from the
+        // user's immutable loop variable, so assigning that is E0060 and
+        // cannot corrupt the trip count.
+        let counter = fcx.new_local_unscoped("__i", TyInt, true, span)
+        let end = fcx.new_local_unscoped("__end", TyInt, false, span)
+        fcx.scopes.push(Map::new())
+        let i = self.for_loop_binding(fcx, pattern, TyInt)
+        fcx.loop_depth += 1
+        let body_hir = self.check_block(fcx, body.value, body.span)
+        fcx.loop_depth -= 1
+        let _ = fcx.scopes.pop()
+        // The immutable loop variable bound to the counter each iteration.
+        let bind_i = loop_bind(i, read_int(counter, span), span)
+        // `__i = __i + 1`
+        let incr = assign_to(
+            counter,
+            HirExpr {
+                kind: EkBinary(
+                    OpAdd,
+                    read_int(counter, span),
+                    HirExpr { kind: EkIntLit(1), ty: TyInt, span: span },
+                ),
+                ty: TyInt,
+                span: span,
+            },
+            span,
+        )
+        let mut outer: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+        outer.push(let_stmt(counter, lo, span))
+        outer.push(let_stmt(end, hi, span))
+        let while_expr = if inclusive {
+            // An inclusive range uses a run flag, so that iterating up to
+            // `Int::MAX` ends instead of wrapping past the bound.
+            let run = fcx.new_local_unscoped("__run", TyBool, true, span)
+            outer.push(let_stmt(run, compare(OpLe, counter, end, span), span))
+            // The counter and the flag advance before the body, so that a
+            // `continue` still progresses.
+            let update_run = assign_to(run, compare(OpLt, counter, end, span), span)
+            let mut stmts: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+            stmts.push(bind_i)
+            stmts.push(update_run)
+            stmts.push(incr)
+            stmts.push(body_hir)
+            let while_body = HirExpr { kind: EkBlock(stmts, None), ty: TyUnit, span: span }
+            HirExpr {
+                kind: EkWhile(HirExpr { kind: EkLocal(run), ty: TyBool, span: span }, while_body),
+                ty: TyUnit,
+                span: span,
+            }
+        } else {
+            let cond = compare(OpLt, counter, end, span)
+            // The increment before the body, so `continue` still advances.
+            let mut stmts: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+            stmts.push(bind_i)
+            stmts.push(incr)
+            stmts.push(body_hir)
+            let while_body = HirExpr { kind: EkBlock(stmts, None), ty: TyUnit, span: span }
+            HirExpr { kind: EkWhile(cond, while_body), ty: TyUnit, span: span }
+        }
+        outer.push(while_expr)
+        HirExpr { kind: EkBlock(outer, None), ty: TyUnit, span: span }
+    }
+
+    // `for x in it { body }` over an array or a value whose type has an
+    // `Iterator`-shaped `next` (`check_for_iterator`): `{ let mut __it = it
+    // while true { match __it.next() { Some(x) => { body }, None => break } }
+    // }`. `__it` is unscoped and `mut`, so `next`'s `mut self` is met; the
+    // user's `x` stays immutable.
+    fn check_for_iterator(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        pattern: Spanned<Pattern>,
+        iter: Spanned<Expr>,
+        body: Spanned<Block>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let it_name = "__it"
+        let iterable = self.check_expr(fcx, iter)
+        let iter_ty = fcx.icx.apply(iterable.ty)
+        // The iterable's own mistake is already reported.
+        match iter_ty {
+            TyError => return error_expr(span)
+            TyArray(elem) => return self.check_for_array(fcx, pattern, iterable, elem, body, span)
+            _ => ()
+        }
+        let next = match self.iterator_next(fcx, iter_ty) {
+            Some(n) => n
+            None => {
+                self.unsupported(
+                    iter.span,
+                    "`for` loops over anything but an integer range (`a..b`), an array, or a value implementing `Iterator` (try `.iter()`)",
+                )
+                return error_expr(span)
+            }
+        }
+        let it_local = fcx.new_local_unscoped(it_name, iter_ty, true, span)
+        let receiver = HirExpr { kind: EkLocal(it_local), ty: iter_ty, span: iter.span }
+        // `emit_trait_call` classifies its receiver by `place_root`, which
+        // resolves an AST name in the scopes: the receiver is spelt as a
+        // path, findable for the one call emitted here.
+        let it_ast = Spanned::new(
+            ExprPath(single_path(Spanned::new(it_name, iter.span))),
+            iter.span,
+        )
+        let mut scope: Map<String, Int> = Map::new()
+        let _ = scope.insert(it_name, it_local)
+        fcx.scopes.push(scope)
+        let next_call = self.emit_trait_call(
+            fcx,
+            next.trait_id,
+            next.method_idx,
+            TraitCallSelfReceiver(receiver, it_ast),
+            Vec::new(),
+            span,
+        )
+        let _ = fcx.scopes.pop()
+        // The item type is read off the call's result, whose projection the
+        // call already normalized against the impl it selected.
+        let item_ty = match fcx.icx.apply(next_call.ty) {
+            TySum(def_id, args) => if def_id == next.option {
+                self.some_payload(next, args)
+            } else {
+                TyError
+            }
+            // `emit_trait_call` bailed, having said why.
+            _ => TyError
+        }
+        fcx.scopes.push(Map::new())
+        let elem = self.for_loop_binding(fcx, pattern, item_ty)
+        fcx.loop_depth += 1
+        let body_hir = self.check_block(fcx, body.value, body.span)
+        fcx.loop_depth -= 1
+        let _ = fcx.scopes.pop()
+        let mut some_fields: Vec<HirPattern> = Vec::new()
+        some_fields.push(loop_bind_pattern(elem))
+        let mut stmts: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+        stmts.push(body_hir)
+        let mut arms: Vec<HirArm> = Vec::new()
+        // The body in a block, so the arm is `()` whatever its value.
+        arms.push(
+            HirArm {
+                pattern: PatVariant(next.option, next.some, some_fields),
+                guard: None,
+                body: HirExpr { kind: EkBlock(stmts, None), ty: TyUnit, span: span },
+                span: body.span,
+            },
+        )
+        arms.push(
+            HirArm {
+                pattern: PatVariant(next.option, next.none, Vec::new()),
+                guard: None,
+                body: HirExpr { kind: EkBreak, ty: TyNever, span: span },
+                span: span,
+            },
+        )
+        let while_expr = HirExpr {
+            kind: EkWhile(
+                HirExpr { kind: EkBoolLit(true), ty: TyBool, span: span },
+                HirExpr { kind: EkMatch(next_call, arms), ty: TyUnit, span: span },
+            ),
+            ty: TyUnit,
+            span: span,
+        }
+        let bind_it = HirExpr { kind: EkLet(it_local, iterable), ty: TyUnit, span: span }
+        let mut outer: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+        outer.push(bind_it)
+        outer.push(while_expr)
+        HirExpr { kind: EkBlock(outer, None), ty: TyUnit, span: span }
+    }
+
+    // The payload type of `next`'s `Some`, at the sum's arguments `args`.
+    fn some_payload(self, next: IteratorNext, args: Vec<Ty>) -> Ty {
+        for s in self.sums.iter() {
+            if s.def_id == next.option {
+                if next.some < 0 || next.some >= s.variants.len() { return TyError }
+                let v = s.variants.at(next.some)
+                if v.fields.is_empty() { return TyError }
+                return subst(v.fields.at(0), args)
+            }
+        }
+        TyError
+    }
+
+    // The `next` a `for` loop drives on a value of type `recv_ty`: none when
+    // the type has no method of that name, more than one trait provides
+    // one, or the one found is not shaped like `Iterator::next`
+    // (`iterator_next`).
+    fn iterator_next(self, fcx: FnCtx, recv_ty: Ty) -> Option<IteratorNext> {
+        let (trait_id, method_idx) = match self.resolve_method_on(recv_ty, fcx, "next") {
+            MethodResTrait(t, i) => (t, i)
+            _ => return None
+        }
````
