+/// Each root's part of `dump`, by the header line that starts it.
+fn parts_by_root(dump: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
+    let mut parts: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();
+    for line in dump.split_inclusive('\n') {
+        if let Some(root) = line.strip_prefix("== ") {
+            parts.push((
+                root.trim_end_matches(['\n', '\r']).to_string(),
+                String::new(),
+            ));
+        } else if let Some((_, part)) = parts.last_mut() {
+            part.push_str(line);
+        }
+    }
+    parts
+}

-/// `dump` is well formed, as the grammar's nesting has it (ADR 0055 §2,
-/// ADR 0056): after each `== ` header, an `IOERR` line or a part whose
-/// every line starts two spaces deeper for each node still open and with
-/// `(`, whose parentheses outside the quotes never close more than is open
-/// and balance by the part's end, and whose quotes close on their line.
-fn assert_well_formed(dump: &str) {
-    let mut depth = 0usize;
-    let mut part = "";
-    for (n, line) in dump.lines().enumerate() {
-        if line.starts_with("== ") || line.starts_with("IOERR ") {
-            assert_eq!(depth, 0, "{part}: a node open before line {n}");
-            part = line;
-            continue;
-        }
-        let indent = line.len() - line.trim_start_matches(' ').len();
-        assert!(
-            indent == 2 * depth && line[indent..].starts_with('('),
-            "{part}: line {n} at depth {depth}: {line}"
-        );
-        let mut quoted = false;
-        for c in line[indent..].chars() {
-            match c {
-                '"' => quoted = !quoted,
-                '(' if !quoted => depth += 1,
-                ')' if !quoted => {
-                    assert!(depth > 0, "{part}: line {n} closes too much: {line}");
-                    depth -= 1;
-                }
-                _ => {}
-            }
-        }
-        assert!(!quoted, "{part}: line {n} leaves a quote open: {line}");
-    }
-    assert_eq!(depth, 0, "{part}: a node open at the end");
-}

-/// Each root's part of `dump`, by the header line that starts it.
-fn parts_by_root(dump: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
-    let mut parts: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();
-    for line in dump.split_inclusive('\n') {
-        if let Some(root) = line.strip_prefix("== ") {
-            parts.push((
-                root.trim_end_matches(['\n', '\r']).to_string(),
-                String::new(),
-            ));
-        } else if let Some((_, part)) = parts.last_mut() {
-            part.push_str(line);
-        }
-    }
-    parts
-}

-/// What N's full dump gave for one input, against the list.

-struct BodiesCompared {

-    refused: Vec<((String, String), String)>,
-    unlisted: Vec<String>,
-    differ: Vec<String>,
-}
-
-/// One set of inputs, `roots` relative to `dir` under `mode`, each named
-/// `prefix` and its root in the list: N's full `hir` on every root, then
-/// S0's `check --dump-hir` on the roots N gives, in batches.
-fn n_bodies_on(
-    mode: Mode,
-    dir: &Path,
-    roots: &[String],
-    prefix: &str,
-    listed: &std::collections::BTreeSet<(String, String)>,
-) -> BodiesCompared {
-    let std_dir = std_dir();
-    let mut n_args = vec!["hir", "--std", std_dir.as_str()];
-    n_args.extend(mode.flags());
-    let s0_args: Vec<&str> = HIR_S0.iter().chain(mode.flags()).copied().collect();
-    let mut out = BodiesCompared::default();
-    for chunk in roots.chunks(BATCH) {
-        let n = run(selfhost(), &n_args, dir, chunk).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{e}"));
-        let n_text = String::from_utf8(n.stdout).expect("N's dump is UTF-8");
-        let n_parts = parts_by_root(&n_text);
-        let names: Vec<&str> = n_parts.iter().map(|(r, _)| r.as_str()).collect();
-        assert_eq!(names, chunk, "N's headers, {}: {}", dir.display(), n.stderr);
-        let refused = n_parts
-            .iter()
-            .filter(|(_, p)| p.starts_with("UNPORTED "))
-            .count();
-        assert_eq!(
-            n.code,
-            Some(if refused > 0 { 3 } else { 0 }),
-            "N on {chunk:?}: {}",
-            n.stderr
-        );
-        let given: Vec<String> = n_parts
-            .iter()
-            .filter(|(_, p)| !p.starts_with("UNPORTED "))
-            .map(|(r, _)| r.clone())
-            .collect();
-        let s0_parts = if given.is_empty() {
-            Vec::new()
-        } else {
-            let s0 = run(&nova(), &s0_args, dir, &given).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{e}"));
-            assert_eq!(s0.code, Some(0), "S0 on {given:?}: {}", s0.stderr);
-            parts_by_root(&String::from_utf8(s0.stdout).expect("S0's dump is UTF-8"))
-        };
-        let mut s0_parts = s0_parts.into_iter();
-        for (root, part) in n_parts {
-            let input = format!("{prefix}{root}");
-            let key = (mode_name(mode).to_string(), input.clone());
-            if let Some(why) = part.strip_prefix("UNPORTED ") {
-                out.refused.push((key, why.trim_end().to_string()));
-                continue;
-            }
-            let (s0_root, s0_part) = s0_parts.next().expect("S0's part");
-            assert_eq!(s0_root, root);
-            if !listed.contains(&key) {
-                out.unlisted.push(format!("{} {input}", key.0));
-            } else if s0_part != part {
-                let at = first_difference(s0_part.as_bytes(), part.as_bytes());
-                out.differ.push(format!("{} {input}: {at:?}", key.0));
-            } else {
-                out.agree += 1;
-            }
-        }
-    }
-    out
-}

+record P { x: Int }
+trait Make { fn make() -> Int }
+trait Build { fn make() -> Int }
+type Color = | Red | Green
+fn bit_not(n: Int) -> Int { ~n }
+fn unknown_field() -> P { P { x: 1, y: 2 } }
+fn both<T: Make + Build>(t: T) -> Int { T::make() }
+fn closure_ret() -> Int {
+    let f = |x: Int| -> Bool { x }
+    1
+}
+fn not_a_variant(o: Option<Int>) -> Int {
+    match o {
+        Some(x) => x
+        Red => 0
+    }
+}
+impl P {
+    fn set(self) {
+        self = P { x: 2 }
+    }
+}
+fn main() {}

+/// Functions [`body_mutate`] appends, `{n}` replaced by a number of the

+    ("E0001", "fn fz_unknown{n}() -> Int { fz_nowhere{n} }"),
+    ("E0001", "fn fz_nocall{n}() -> Int { fz_absent{n}(1) }"),
+    ("E0010", "fn fz_ret{n}() -> Int { \"fz\" }"),
+    ("E0010", "fn fz_let{n}() {\n    let x: Bool = 1\n}"),
+    ("E0011", "fn fz_infer{n}() {\n    let v = []\n}"),
+    ("E0011", "fn fz_none{n}() {\n    let o = None\n}"),
+    ("E0013", "fn fz_op{n}() -> Bool { true + false }"),
+    ("E0013", "fn fz_show{n}(f: fn() -> Int) { println(\"${f}\") }"),

+    ("E0016", "fn fz_variant{n}() -> Option<Int> { Some(1, 2) }"),
+    ("E0020", "fn fz_match{n}(o: Option<Int>) -> Int {\n    match o {\n        Some(x) => x\n    }\n}"),
+    ("E0021", "fn fz_unreach{n}(x: Int) -> Int {\n    match x {\n        _ => 0\n        1 => 1\n    }\n}"),
+    ("E0022", "fn fz_refute{n}(o: Option<Int>) -> Int {\n    let Some(x) = o\n    x\n}"),
+    ("E0060", "fn fz_imm{n}() {\n    let x = 1\n    x = 2\n}"),
+    ("E0080", "fn fz_break{n}() {\n    break\n}"),
+    ("E0080", "fn fz_continue{n}() {\n    continue\n}"),
+    ("E0081", "const FZ_A{n}: Int = FZ_B{n}\nconst FZ_B{n}: Int = FZ_A{n}"),

+    ("E0099", "fn fz_ret_try{n}(o: Option<Int>) -> Int { o? }"),

+/// What [`body_mutate`] edits in place, inside the functions' and methods'
+/// bodies alone: by the tokens there.
+#[derive(Default)]
+struct BodySites {
+    /// Each body's span, its braces included, and whether its function is
+    /// `async`.
+    bodies: Vec<(Range, bool)>,
+    /// Integer literals, each in an `async` body or not.
+    ints: Vec<(Range, bool)>,
+    /// String literals without interpolation, `"` to `"`, and `true` and
+    /// `false`.
+    literals: Vec<Range>,
+    /// Each call's or method call's argument list, `(` to `)`, and where
+    /// its last argument starts (after the last top-level comma, or the
+    /// `(`), `None` for no argument.
+    calls: Vec<(Range, Option<usize>)>,
+    /// A field's name after a `.`, not called.
+    fields: Vec<Range>,
+    /// A method's name after a `.`, called.
+    methods: Vec<Range>,
+    /// A one-line `match` arm: its line, through its line break.
+    arms: Vec<Range>,
+    /// The `mut ` of a `let mut`.
+    muts: Vec<Range>,
+    /// A `let`'s annotation, from its `:` up to the space before its `=`.
+    annotations: Vec<Range>,
+}
+
+fn body_sites(source: &str) -> Option<BodySites> {
+    use nova_ast::Item;
+    use nova_lexer::Token;
+    let (tokens, lex_errors) = nova_lexer::lex(source, FileId::DUMMY);
+    if !lex_errors.is_empty() {
+        return None;
+    }
+    let parsed = nova_parser::parse_recovering(&tokens, FileId::DUMMY);
+    if !parsed.errors.is_empty() {
+        return None;
+    }
+    let mut sites = BodySites::default();
+    let body = |f: &nova_ast::item::Function| {
+        (
+            (f.body.span.start as usize, f.body.span.end as usize),
+            f.is_async,
+        )
+    };
+    for item in &parsed.file.items {
+        match &item.value {
+            Item::Function(f) => sites.bodies.push(body(f)),
+            Item::Impl(b) => sites.bodies.extend(b.functions.iter().map(body)),
+            _ => {}
+        }
+    }
+    let toks: Vec<(Token, Range)> = tokens
+        .iter()
+        .map(|t| {
+            (
+                t.value.clone(),
+                (t.span.start as usize, t.span.end as usize),
+            )
+        })
+        .collect();
+    let in_body = |at: usize| sites.bodies.iter().find(|((s, e), _)| *s < at && at < *e);
+    let line_end = |at: usize| source[at..].find('\n').map_or(source.len(), |i| at + i + 1);
+    let mut ints = Vec::new();
+    let mut literals = Vec::new();
+    let mut calls = Vec::new();
+    let mut fields = Vec::new();
+    let mut methods = Vec::new();
+    let mut arms = Vec::new();
+    let mut muts = Vec::new();
+    let mut annotations = Vec::new();
+    for (i, (tok, (start, end))) in toks.iter().enumerate() {
+        let Some((_, is_async)) = in_body(*start) else {
+            continue;
+        };
+        let next = toks.get(i + 1).map(|t| &t.0);
+        let prev = i.checked_sub(1).map(|j| &toks[j].0);
+        match tok {
+            Token::Int(_) if prev != Some(&Token::Dot) => ints.push(((*start, *end), *is_async)),
+            Token::True | Token::False => literals.push((*start, *end)),
+            Token::StrStart if matches!(toks.get(i + 2), Some((Token::StrEnd, _))) => {
+                if let (Some(Token::StrPart(_)), Some((_, (_, close)))) = (next, toks.get(i + 2)) {
+                    literals.push((*start, *close));
+                }
+            }
+            Token::Ident(_) if prev == Some(&Token::Dot) => {
+                if next == Some(&Token::LParen) {
+                    methods.push((*start, *end));
+                } else {
+                    fields.push((*start, *end));
+                }
+            }
+            Token::LParen if matches!(prev, Some(Token::Ident(_))) => {
+                // The matching `)`, and the last top-level comma.
+                let mut depth = 0usize;
+                let mut last = None;
+                for (k, (tok, (_, e))) in toks.iter().enumerate().skip(i) {
+                    match tok {
+                        Token::LParen | Token::LBracket | Token::LBrace | Token::InterpOpen => {
+                            depth += 1
+                        }
+                        Token::RParen | Token::RBracket | Token::RBrace | Token::InterpClose => {
+                            depth -= 1;
+                            if depth == 0 {
+                                let args = (k > i + 1).then(|| last.unwrap_or(*end));
+                                calls.push(((*start, *e), args));
+                                break;
+                            }
+                        }
+                        Token::Comma if depth == 1 => last = Some(*e),
+                        _ => {}
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            Token::FatArrow => {
+                let from = line_start(source, *start);
+                let to = line_end(*start);
+                let line = &source[from..to];
+                let balanced = |open: char, close: char| {
+                    line.matches(open).count() == line.matches(close).count()
+                };
+                if !line.contains("match ")
+                    && balanced('(', ')')
+                    && balanced('{', '}')
+                    && balanced('[', ']')
+                {
+                    arms.push((from, to));
+                }
+            }
+            Token::Let if next == Some(&Token::Mut) => {
+                let (s, _) = toks[i + 1].1;
+                let (n, _) = toks[i + 2].1;
+                muts.push((s, n));
+            }
+            Token::Colon
+                if matches!(prev, Some(Token::Ident(_)))
+                    && (matches!(toks.get(i.wrapping_sub(2)), Some((Token::Let, _)))
+                        || matches!(toks.get(i.wrapping_sub(2)), Some((Token::Mut, _)))) =>
+            {
+                // Up to the `=` on the same line.
+                let eq = toks[i..].iter().position(|t| t.0 == Token::Eq);
+                if let Some(k) = eq {
+                    let (eq_start, _) = toks[i + k].1;
+                    if !source[*start..eq_start].contains('\n') {
+                        annotations.push((*start, source[..eq_start].trim_end().len()));
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            _ => {}
+        }
+    }
+    sites.ints = ints;
+    sites.literals = literals;
+    sites.calls = calls;
+    sites.fields = fields;
+    sites.methods = methods;
+    sites.arms = arms;
+    sites.muts = muts;
+    sites.annotations = annotations;
+    Some(sites)
+}
+
+/// `source`, a program that checks clean, mutated one to three times
+/// inside its bodies (module docs, 6.): an integer, a string or a `true`
+/// made a value of another type, an argument added to a call or its last
+/// one dropped, a field or a method renamed, a one-line `match` arm
+/// deleted, an integer given `?` or `.await`, a `let mut` made `let`, a
+/// `let`'s annotation removed, `break` put first in a body, or one of
+/// [`BODY_ITEMS`] appended, numbered from `n`. A mutation that would not
+/// parse is skipped; a mutation renames nothing an item declares, and
+/// every name an appended item declares is new, so every input reaches the
+/// type checker, which the harness checks.
+pub fn body_mutate(rng: &mut SplitMix64, source: &str, n: usize) -> String {
+    let mut text = source.to_string();
+    for step in 0..1 + rng.below(3) {
+        let Some(sites) = body_sites(&text) else {
+            break;
+        };
+        let splice =
+            |(start, end): Range, with: &str| format!("{}{with}{}", &text[..start], &text[end..]);
+        let edited = match rng.below(16) {
+            0 if !sites.ints.is_empty() => {
+                let ((s, e), _) = *rng.pick(&sites.ints);
+                Some(splice((s, e), rng.pick(&["\"fz\"", "1.5", "true", "'z'"])))
+            }
+            1 if !sites.literals.is_empty() => Some(splice(
+                *rng.pick(&sites.literals),
+                rng.pick(&["1", "[1]", "()"]),
+            )),
+            2 if !sites.calls.is_empty() => {
+                // An argument added.
+                let ((_, close), last) = *rng.pick(&sites.calls);
+                let with = if last.is_some() { ", 1" } else { "1" };
+                Some(splice((close - 1, close - 1), with))
+            }
+            3 if sites.calls.iter().any(|c| c.1.is_some()) => {
+                // The last argument dropped, with its comma.
+                let with_args: Vec<&(Range, Option<usize>)> =
+                    sites.calls.iter().filter(|c| c.1.is_some()).collect();
+                let &&((open, close), last) = rng.pick(&with_args);
+                let from = last.unwrap_or(open + 1);
+                let from = if from == open + 1 {
+                    from
+                } else {
+                    text[..from].rfind(',').unwrap_or(from)
+                };
+                Some(splice((from, close - 1), ""))
+            }
+            4 if !sites.fields.is_empty() => {
+                let (s, e) = *rng.pick(&sites.fields);
+                let renamed = format!("fz_{}", &text[s..e]);
+                Some(splice((s, e), &renamed))
+            }
+            5 if !sites.methods.is_empty() => {
+                let (s, e) = *rng.pick(&sites.methods);
+                let renamed = format!("fz_{}", &text[s..e]);
+                Some(splice((s, e), &renamed))
+            }
+            6 | 7 if !sites.arms.is_empty() => Some(splice(*rng.pick(&sites.arms), "")),
+            8 if !sites.ints.is_empty() => {
+                let ((s, e), _) = *rng.pick(&sites.ints);
+                let with = format!("({})?", &text[s..e]);
+                Some(splice((s, e), &with))
+            }
+            9 if sites.ints.iter().any(|i| !i.1) => {
+                // In a function that is not `async`.
+                let plain: Vec<Range> = sites.ints.iter().filter(|i| !i.1).map(|i| i.0).collect();
+                let (s, e) = *rng.pick(&plain);
+                let with = format!("({}).await", &text[s..e]);
+                Some(splice((s, e), &with))
+            }
+            10 if !sites.muts.is_empty() => Some(splice(*rng.pick(&sites.muts), "")),
+            11 if !sites.annotations.is_empty() => Some(splice(*rng.pick(&sites.annotations), "")),
+            12 if !sites.bodies.is_empty() => {
+                let ((s, _), _) = *rng.pick(&sites.bodies);
+                Some(splice((s + 1, s + 1), "\n    break\n"))
+            }
+            _ => {
+                let (_, item) = rng.pick(&BODY_ITEMS);
+                let item = item.replace("{n}", &format!("{n}x{step}"));
+                Some(format!("{}\n{item}\n", text.trim_end_matches('\n')))
+            }
+        };
+        if let Some(next) = edited {
+            if body_sites(&next).is_some() {
+                text = next;
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    text
+}
+
+/// The kinds of nesting [`body_deep`] writes for the type checker's bodies
+/// (5.3b, spec §4.6, ADR 0056 §12), beside [`DEEP_KINDS`], each with the
+/// deepest level the parser takes, at most its limit, 128: closures in
+/// closures (called at once, capturing, with parameters), arrays,
+/// indexing, tuples, interpolation, method chains, `?`, a `let`'s
+/// annotation, tuple, variant, or- and `let` patterns, `match` in an arm
+/// and as a scrutinee, and `for` over a range, an array and with a tuple
+/// pattern. A closure called at once, `(|| e)()`, is two of the parser's
+/// levels, its parentheses and the closure, so 64 of them are 128 levels;
+/// a `match` arm's pattern starts a level in, the arm's own, so 127
+/// patterns nest there; and 127 `for` loops nest around the statement in
+/// the innermost, a level of its own.
+pub const BODY_DEEP_KINDS: [(&str, usize); 19] = [
+    ("closures", 64),
+    ("closure-captures", 64),
+    ("closure-params", 64),
+    ("arrays", 128),
+    ("indexes", 128),
+    ("tuples", 128),
+    ("interpolations", 128),
+    ("method-chains", 128),
+    ("questions", 128),
+    ("annotations", 128),
+    ("tuple-patterns", 127),
+    ("variant-patterns", 127),
+    ("or-patterns", 128),
+    ("let-patterns", 128),
+    ("match-arms", 128),
+    ("match-scrutinees", 128),
+    ("for-ranges", 127),
+    ("for-arrays", 127),
+    ("for-patterns", 127),
+];
+
+/// A program nested `depth` times as `kind` names ([`BODY_DEEP_KINDS`]),
+/// which type-checks with no diagnostic.
+pub fn body_deep(kind: &str, depth: usize) -> String {
+    let d = depth;
+    let wrap = |open: &str, inner: &str, close: &str, n: usize| {
+        format!("{}{inner}{}", open.repeat(n), close.repeat(n))
+    };
+    let main = |body: String| format!("fn main() {{\n    {body}\n}}\n");
+    let value = |x: String| main(format!("let x = {x}\n    println(\"${{x}}\")"));
+    let function = |f: String| format!("{f}\n\nfn main() {{}}\n");
+    // `open(k)` for k from `d - 1` down to 0, and `close(k)` from 0 up.
+    let nest = |open: &dyn Fn(usize) -> String, close: &dyn Fn(usize) -> String| {
+        let opens: String = (0..d).rev().map(open).collect();
+        let closes: String = (0..d).map(close).collect();
+        (opens, closes)
+    };
+    match kind {
+        "closures" => value(wrap("(|| ", "1", ")()", d)),
+        "closure-captures" => main(format!(
+            "let y = 1\n    let x = {}\n    println(\"${{x}}\")",
+            wrap("(|| ", "y", ")()", d)
+        )),
+        "closure-params" => {
+            let (o, c) = nest(&|k| format!("(|a{k}: Int| "), &|k| format!(")({k})"));
+            value(format!("{o}a0{c}"))
+        }
+        "arrays" => main(format!("let x = {}\n    let _y = x", wrap("[", "1", "]", d))),
+        "indexes" => value(format!("{}{}", wrap("[", "1", "]", d), "[0]".repeat(d))),
+        "tuples" => main(format!("let x = {}\n    let _y = x", wrap("(", "1", ",)", d))),
+        "interpolations" => value(wrap("\"${", "1", "}\"", d)),
+        "method-chains" => main(format!(
+            "let s = \"a\"\n    let x = s{}\n    println(\"${{x}}\")",
+            ".trim()".repeat(d)
+        )),
+        "questions" => function(format!(
+            "fn f(o: Option<Int>) -> Option<Int> {{\n    let x = {}\n    Some(x)\n}}",
+            wrap("Some(", "o?", ")?", d)
+        )),
+        "annotations" => main(format!(
+            "let x: {} = None\n    let _y = x",
+            wrap("Option<", "Int", ">", d)
+        )),
+        "tuple-patterns" => main(format!(
+            "match {} {{\n        {} => println(\"${{x}}\")\n    }}",
+            wrap("(", "1", ",)", d),
+            wrap("(", "x", ",)", d)
+        )),
+        "variant-patterns" => main(format!(
+            "let v = {}\n    match v {{\n        {} => println(\"${{x}}\")\n        _ => ()\n    }}",
+            wrap("Some(", "1", ")", d),
+            wrap("Some(", "x", ")", d)
+        )),
+        "or-patterns" => {
+            let alternatives: String = (2..=d).map(|k| format!(" | {k})")).collect();
+            function(format!(
+                "fn f(x: Int) -> Int {{\n    match x {{\n        {}1{alternatives} => 1\n        _ => 0\n    }}\n}}",
+                "(".repeat(d - 1)
+            ))
+        }
+        "let-patterns" => function(format!(
+            "fn f(x: {}) -> Int {{\n    let {} = x\n    n\n}}",
+            wrap("(", "Int", ", Int)", d),
+            wrap("(", "n", ", _)", d)
+        )),
+        "match-arms" => {
+            let (o, c) = nest(&|k| format!("match x {{ {k} => "), &|_| ", _ => 1 }".to_string());
+            function(format!("fn f(x: Int) -> Int {{ {o}0{c} }}"))
+        }
+        "match-scrutinees" => function(format!(
+            "fn f(x: Int) -> Int {{ {}x{} }}",
+            "match ".repeat(d),
+            " { 0 => 1, n => n }".repeat(d)
+        )),
+        "for-ranges" | "for-arrays" | "for-patterns" => {
+            let (param, head): (&str, &dyn Fn(usize) -> String) = match kind {
+                "for-ranges" => ("", &|k| format!("for i{k} in 0..2 {{ ")),
+                "for-arrays" => ("a: [Int]", &|k| format!("for i{k} in a {{ ")),
+                _ => ("v: [(Int, Int)]", &|k| format!("for (p{k}, q{k}) in v {{ ")),
+            };
+            let (o, c) = nest(head, &|_| " }".to_string());
+            function(format!(
+                "fn f({param}) -> Int {{\n    let mut t = 0\n    {o}t += 1{c}\n    t\n}}"
+            ))
+        }
+        other => panic!("no kind of nesting {other}"),
+    }
+}

+++ b/selfhost/src/typeck_view.nova
@@ -0,0 +1,377 @@
+// The type checker's views: a port of check/view.rs (`ui`,
+// `component_ret`, `check_view`, `view_node`, `view_text`, `element`,
+// `element_builder`, `view_attr`, `view_handler`, `reader`, `ui_variant`,
+// and the free `text_child`, `is_str_lit`, `sum`, `str_lit` and `array`),
+// function by function and with the same names (spec
+// docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-phase-5-3-the-type-checker-and-hir-design.md
+// §4.2, ADR 0056). typeck_body.nova gives the idioms.
+//
+// `view { … }` and `component` (RFC 0001): a view's elements, text and
+// attributes become the calls and variants of `std/ui`'s API here, as
+// string interpolation becomes calls; no pass rewrites the tree before
+// this one. S0's `note_use` calls are the language server's index, which
+// N does not port.
+
+import ast
+import hir
+import infer
+import resolver
+import token
+import typeck
+import typeck_body
+import typeck_call
+import typeck_closure
+import typeck_expr
+
+/// What a view desugars to (`Ui`): `std/ui`'s two sums, `View` and
+/// `Attr`, and the two builders of `std/ui/html` it calls or shows, `on(kind,
+/// f)`, which adapts a `fn()` handler to `On`'s `fn(String)`, and `text`.
+pub record Ui { pub view: Int, pub attr: Int, pub on: Int, pub text: Int }
+
+impl Checker {
+    /// `std/ui`'s names, which every target compiles, so a view needs no
+    /// import of its own (`ui`).
+    pub fn ui(self) -> Option<Ui> {
+        let ui = self.module_named("$std.ui")
+        if ui < 0 { return None }
+        let html = self.module_named("$std.ui.html")
+        if html < 0 { return None }
+        let view = self.resolve_type_in(ui, "View")
+        if view < 0 { return None }
+        let attr = self.resolve_type_in(ui, "Attr")
+        if attr < 0 { return None }
+        let on = self.def_value(html, "on")
+        if on < 0 { return None }
+        let text = self.def_value(html, "text")
+        if text < 0 { return None }
+        Some(Ui { view: view, attr: attr, on: on, text: text })
+    }
+
+    // The first module named `name`, or -1.
+    fn module_named(self, name: String) -> Int {
+        for m in 0..self.defs.modules.len() { if self.defs.modules.at(m).name == name { return m } }
+        -1
+    }
+
+    // The definition the value `name` in module `m` names, or -1.
+    fn def_value(self, m: Int, name: String) -> Int {
+        match self.resolve_value_in(m, name) {
+            Some(ResDef(id)) => id
+            _ => -1
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// A component's return type: `std/ui`'s `View` (`component_ret`).
+    pub fn component_ret(self) -> Ty {
+        match self.ui() {
+            Some(ui) => sum(ui.view)
+            None => TyError
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// `view { child }`: the `View` its one child desugars to
+    /// (`check_view`).
+    pub fn check_view(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        children: Vec<Spanned<ViewNode>>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let ui = match self.ui() {
+            Some(u) => u
+            None => return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        if children.len() != 1 {
+            self.error("E0094", "`view` holds one root, found ${children.len()}", span)
+            for c in children.iter() { let _ = self.view_node(fcx, ui, c) }
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        self.view_node(fcx, ui, children.at(0))
+    }
+
+    // A child: an element, a view's `text(…)`, or an expression of type
+    // `View` (`view_node`).
+    fn view_node(mut self, mut fcx: FnCtx, ui: Ui, node: Spanned<ViewNode>) -> HirExpr {
+        match node.value {
+            ViewNodeElement(name, args, children) => self.element(
+                fcx,
+                ui,
+                name,
+                args,
+                children,
+                node.span,
+            )
+            ViewNodeExpr(e) => {
+                match text_child(e) {
+                    Some((_, content)) => return self.view_text(fcx, ui, content, e.span)
+                    None => ()
+                }
+                let x = self.check_expr(fcx, e)
+                self.expect_ty(fcx, x, sum(ui.view), "a view's child")
+                x
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    // `text(e)`: `Text(e)` for a string literal, `DynText(|| e)` for
+    // anything else (`view_text`).
+    fn view_text(mut self, mut fcx: FnCtx, ui: Ui, content: Spanned<Expr>, span: Span) -> HirExpr {
+        if is_str_lit(content) {
+            let v = self.check_expr(fcx, content)
+            return self.ui_variant(fcx, ui.view, "Text", Vec::from_array([v]), span)
+        }
+        let (f, ty) = self.reader(fcx, content)
+        if !fcx.icx.unify(ty, TyString) {
+            self.error(
+                "E0010",
+                "text must have type `String`, found `${self.show(ty, fcx)}`",
+                content.span,
+            )
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        self.ui_variant(fcx, ui.view, "DynText", Vec::from_array([f]), span)
+    }
+
+    // An element: a call of its builder with its attributes and its
+    // children (`element`).
+    fn element(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        ui: Ui,
+        name: Spanned<String>,
+        args: Vec<ViewArg>,
+        children: Option<Vec<Spanned<ViewNode>>>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let builder = self.element_builder(fcx, ui, name)
+        let mut attrs: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+        for a in args.iter() { attrs.push(self.view_attr(fcx, ui, a)) }
+        let mut kids: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+        match children {
+            Some(cs) => { for c in cs.iter() { kids.push(self.view_node(fcx, ui, c)) } }
+            None => ()
+        }
+        let (def_id, takes_children) = match builder {
+            Some(b) => b
+            None => return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        if !takes_children && children.is_some() {
+            self.error("E0095", "`${name.value}` takes no children", name.span)
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        let mut call_args: Vec<HirExpr> = Vec::new()
+        call_args.push(array(attrs, sum(ui.attr), span))
+        if takes_children { call_args.push(array(kids, sum(ui.view), span)) }
+        HirExpr {
+            kind: EkCall(CalleeDef(def_id), Vec::new(), call_args),
+            ty: sum(ui.view),
+            span: span,
+        }
+    }
+
+    // The function an element names, and whether it takes children: one
+    // that takes `([Attr], [View])`, or `([Attr])`, and returns `View`
+    // (`element_builder`).
+    fn element_builder(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        ui: Ui,
+        name: Spanned<String>,
+    ) -> Option<(Int, Bool)> {
+        let n = name.value
+        if fcx.lookup(n) >= 0 { return self.not_builder(name) }
+        let def_id = match self.resolve_value_in(self.cur_module, n) {
+            Some(ResDef(id)) => {
+                match self.kind_of(id) {
+                    DefKindFn(_) => id
+                    _ => return self.not_builder(name)
+                }
+            }
+            None => {
+                if !self.missing_on_target(n, name.span) {
+                    self.error("E0001", "cannot find function `${n}` in this scope", name.span)
+                }
+                return None
+            }
+            Some(_) => return self.not_builder(name)
+        }
+        let sig = match self.sigs.at(def_id) {
+            Some(s) => s
+            None => return None
+        }
+        let attrs = TyArray(sum(ui.attr))
+        let views = TyArray(sum(ui.view))
+        if sig.generics != 0 || !ty_eq(sig.ret, sum(ui.view)) { return self.not_builder(name) }
+        if tys_eq(sig.params, Vec::from_array([attrs, views])) {
+            Some((def_id, true))
+        } else if tys_eq(sig.params, Vec::from_array([attrs])) {
+            Some((def_id, false))
+        } else {
+            self.not_builder(name)
+        }
+    }
+
+    // E0096 at an element's name that is not a builder (`element_builder`'s
+    // `not_builder`).
+    fn not_builder(mut self, name: Spanned<String>) -> Option<(Int, Bool)> {
+        self.error(
+            "E0096",
+            "`${name.value}` is not an element builder: one takes `([Attr], [View])` or `([Attr])` and returns `View`",
+            name.span,
+        )
+        None
+    }
+
+    // An element's argument: an `Attr` as it is, or a named one made into
+    // one (`view_attr`).
+    fn view_attr(mut self, mut fcx: FnCtx, ui: Ui, arg: ViewArg) -> HirExpr {
+        let (name, value) = match arg {
+            ViewArgPositional(e) => {
+                let x = self.check_expr(fcx, e)
+                self.expect_ty(fcx, x, sum(ui.attr), "an element's attribute")
+                return x
+            }
+            ViewArgNamed(n, v) => (n, v)
+        }
+        let span = name.span.merge(value.span)
+        if name.value.starts_with("on_") {
+            let kind = name.value.byte_slice(3, name.value.byte_len())
+            if kind.is_empty() {
+                self.error("E0097", "`on_` names no event", name.span)
+                return error_expr(span)
+            }
+            return self.view_handler(fcx, ui, name, kind, value, span)
+        }
+        let key = str_lit("-".join(name.value.split("_")), name.span)
+        let property = name.value == "value"
+        if is_str_lit(value) {
+            let v = self.check_expr(fcx, value)
+            let variant = if property { "Property" } else { "Static" }
+            return self.ui_variant(fcx, ui.attr, variant, Vec::from_array([key, v]), span)
+        }
+        let (f, ty) = self.reader(fcx, value)
+        if !fcx.icx.unify(ty, TyString) {
+            self.error(
+                "E0097",
+                "`${name.value}` takes a `String`, found `${self.show(ty, fcx)}`",
+                value.span,
+            )
+            return error_expr(span)
+        }
+        let variant = if property { "DynProperty" } else { "Dynamic" }
+        self.ui_variant(fcx, ui.attr, variant, Vec::from_array([key, f]), span)
+    }
+
+    // `on_kind: h`: `On("kind", h)` for a `fn(String)`, and `std/ui/html`'s
+    // `on("kind", h)` for a `fn()` (`view_handler`).
+    fn view_handler(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        ui: Ui,
+        name: Spanned<String>,
+        kind: String,
+        value: Spanned<Expr>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let kind = str_lit(kind, name.span)
+        let h = self.check_expr(fcx, value)
+        let other = fcx.icx.apply(h.ty)
+        match other {
+            TyFn(params, ret) => {
+                // S0's guards in order, each unification kept when a later
+                // one fails.
+                if params.is_empty() && fcx.icx.unify(ret, TyUnit) {
+                    return HirExpr {
+                        kind: EkCall(CalleeDef(ui.on), Vec::new(), Vec::from_array([kind, h])),
+                        ty: sum(ui.attr),
+                        span: span,
+                    }
+                }
+                if params.len() == 1
+                    && fcx.icx.unify(params.at(0), TyString)
+                    && fcx.icx.unify(ret, TyUnit) {
+                    return self.ui_variant(fcx, ui.attr, "On", Vec::from_array([kind, h]), span)
+                }
+            }
+            TyError => return error_expr(span)
+            _ => ()
+        }
+        self.error(
+            "E0097",
+            "`${name.value}` takes a handler, `fn()` or `fn(String)`, found `${self.show(other, fcx)}`",
+            value.span,
+        )
+        error_expr(span)
+    }
+
+    // `|| value`, which reads `value` again each time it runs, and the type
+    // `value` has (`reader`).
+    fn reader(mut self, mut fcx: FnCtx, value: Spanned<Expr>) -> (HirExpr, Ty) {
+        let f = self.check_closure(fcx, Vec::new(), None, value, value.span)
+        let ty = match f.ty {
+            TyFn(_, ret) => ret
+            _ => TyError
+        }
+        (f, ty)
+    }
+
+    // The variant `name` of `std/ui`'s sum `sum_id`, made of `args`
+    // (`ui_variant`).
+    fn ui_variant(
+        mut self,
+        mut fcx: FnCtx,
+        sum_id: Int,
+        name: String,
+        args: Vec<HirExpr>,
+        span: Span,
+    ) -> HirExpr {
+        let vi = self.variant_index(sum_id, name)
+        if vi < 0 { return error_expr(span) }
+        self.make_variant(fcx, sum_id, vi, args, span)
+    }
+}
+
+// A child `text(e)`: the bare name `text` and one argument (`text_child`).
+fn text_child(e: Spanned<Expr>) -> Option<(Spanned<String>, Spanned<Expr>)> {
+    let (callee, args) = match e.value {
+        ExprCall(c, a) => (c, a)
+        _ => return None
+    }
+    let path = match callee.value {
+        ExprPath(p) => p
+        _ => return None
+    }
+    if path.segments.len() == 1 && args.len() == 1 && path.segments.at(0).value == "text" {
+        return Some((path.segments.at(0), args.at(0)))
+    }
+    None
+}
+
+// A string literal with no interpolation, which a view keeps fixed: a raw
+// string, or a `StringInterp` of literal parts alone, as the parser makes
+// every other string (`is_str_lit`).
+fn is_str_lit(e: Spanned<Expr>) -> Bool {
+    match e.value {
+        ExprLit(LiteralStr(_)) => true
+        ExprStringInterp(parts) => {
+            for p in parts.iter() {
+                match p {
+                    StringPartLit(_) => ()
+                    _ => return false
+                }
+            }
+            true
+        }
+        _ => false
+    }
+}
+
+fn sum(def_id: Int) -> Ty { TySum(def_id, Vec::new()) }
+
+fn str_lit(s: String, span: Span) -> HirExpr {
+    HirExpr { kind: EkStrLit(s), ty: TyString, span: span }
+}
+
+fn array(elems: Vec<HirExpr>, elem: Ty, span: Span) -> HirExpr {
+    HirExpr { kind: EkMakeArray(elems), ty: TyArray(elem), span: span }
+}
````

  prints them: `the HIR dumps of 251 loose programs, 88 package files, 39

```sh
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$P/plan53b/adrcheck.py")"
cat > "$P/plan53b/adrcheck.py" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""adrcheck.py: run from the repository's root, after the build, with $P exported.
ADR 0056 §2's example against S0's `nova check --dump-hir` of its source.
The block after "One example of every form" is the source, its `;;` lines
(`;; NAME.nova:`, then `;;   ` and a line of the source), then the dump's
lines; the source is written into a fresh directory, the command run there,
and every dump line must be a line of the output, in order. Prints the
verdict and the count of lines found."""
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

P = os.environ["P"]
ADR = "docs/adr/0056-the-self-hosted-type-checker-and-the-full-hir-dump.md"
NOVA = os.path.abspath("target/debug/nova")
text = open(ADR, encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")
start = next(i for i, l in enumerate(text) if l.startswith("**One example of every form**"))
a = next(i for i in range(start, len(text)) if text[i] == "```")
b = next(i for i in range(a + 1, len(text)) if text[i] == "```")
block = text[a + 1 : b]
name = block[0][3:].rstrip(":")
source = [l[5:] for l in block[1:] if l.startswith(";;")]
body = [l for l in block if not l.startswith(";;")]
work = f"{P}/plan53b/adr-ex"
shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
os.makedirs(work)
open(os.path.join(work, name), "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(source) + "\n")
out = subprocess.run([NOVA, "check", "--dump-hir", name], cwd=work, capture_output=True,
                     text=True).stdout.split("\n")
at, missing = 0, None
for line in body:
    while at < len(out) and out[at] != line:
        at += 1
    if at == len(out):
        missing = line
        break
    at += 1
print(f"example: --dump-hir {name}: {len(source)} source lines, {len(body)} dump lines, "
      f"{'ok' if missing is None else 'MISSING ' + repr(missing)}")
sys.exit(1 if missing else 0)
EOF
```

  After the build, `python3 "$P/plan53b/adrcheck.py"`. Expected, as the
  replay printed: `example: --dump-hir forms.nova: 26 source lines, 175
  dump lines, ok`.

  `rm -rf "$P/target-1100"`.

+# ADR 0056 — The self-hosted type checker, and the full HIR dump
+
+## Status
+
+Accepted (2026-11-13). Branch `claude/loving-archimedes-frtf5q-53b`
+(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-phase-5-3-the-type-checker-and-hir-design.md`
+§4), written as 5.3b's prototype was built. Part 1 (S0's side) wrote §1 to §7: S0's order of bodies, the full
+dump's function forms with one example of every form, the closure-id
+rule, std's bodies shared with the fallback and the bug it works around,
+the body cases, the harness's switch, and part 1's figures. Parts 2 to
+4 (N's frame and expressions, members, control flow, patterns and std's
+bodies) wrote §8. Part 5 (views, the harness in its final form, the body
+fuzzer, the depth cases and the figures) wrote §9 to §16 and finished §4,
+§6 and §8. CI's figures (§14) come from the measurement run, draft
+pull request Sakeerin/nova#139, closed unmerged.
+
+## Decision
+
+### 1. S0 checks the program's bodies, then std's, each in `DefId` order
+
+`check_with` (pass 6, `Checker::check_bodies`) checks the program's
+functions, methods and constants, then std's, each in `DefId` order:
+functions, then methods by their sorted ids, then constants. Before, the
+methods came in `FxHashMap` order (`method_locs.keys()`), which put
+eight methods' diagnostics in the order 7 4 1 8 5 2 6 3. The constant
+cycles (E0081) and the newline splits (E0103) follow, then the closures
+and wrappers in the order they were lifted, so the program's take the ids
+from `defs.len()` on and std's follow them.
+
+**What a user sees** (the CHANGELOG's Changed): diagnostics inside
+methods in declaration order, and closures' and wrappers' names
+(`closure$N`, `fnval$N`) renumbered, in symbols only. `nova check` over
+every base-tracked `.nova` file prints what the base prints but for 8
+checks, std's `{bytes,core,dom,http,json,net,strings,time}/lib.nova`
+checked as programs, each the same diagnostics reordered (`checkcmp.sh`
+at 5.3b's last commit; part 1's 11, §7, counted three of N's files
+checked alone, which print alike as 5.3b's later parts leave them). A
+test pins it (`bodies_are_checked_the_programs_first_each_in_def_id_order`).
+
+**Why the program's first** (spec §4.1): std's closures then follow all
+of the program's, so skipping std's bodies (§4) changes no id a program
+prints.
+
+### 2. The full dump
+
+`nova check --dump-hir` prints 5.3a's part (ADR 0055 §2) and then every
+function, after the externs and before the diagnostics; the diagnostics
+are then every diagnostic the type checker gave, the bodies' too. std's
+part (`--std`) adds ` functions=<n>` to its first line. The hidden
+`nova check --dump-hir-items`, by the same parser and refusals, prints
+5.3a's part alone, which the differential compares until N checks bodies
+(§6).
+
+**Order:** a part's own functions in `hir::Module`'s order (§1):
+functions, methods and constants by `DefId`, then the closures and
+wrappers as they were lifted. A function is std's part's when its id is
+std's, or, for a closure or wrapper, when it was lifted from std's
+bodies (§3).
+
+**The grammar** (`I(d)` is `d` levels of indentation; `span` is
+`start..end` in the function's file, or a whole place, label and span,
+should a node be in another file, which none is today):
+
+```
+entries    = { record } { sum } { trait } { impl } { sig } { extern } { function }
+function   = I(1) "(Function " id " " string " generics=" uint " takes_env=" bool
+             " captures=" uint " params=" uint " async=" bool " " place
+             bounds(2) I(2) "(Ret " ty ")" { local } expr(2) ")"
+local      = I(2) "(LocalDecl l" uint " " string " mut=" bool " " span " " ty ")"
+expr(d)    = I(d) "(" kind { " " value } [ " " flag "=" bool ] " " span " " ty
+             [ I(d+1) "(SelfType " ty ")" ] [ I(d+1) "(TypeArgs" { " " ty } ")" ]
+             { expr(d+1) | arm(d+1) } ")"
+arm(d)     = I(d) "(Arm guard=" bool " " span pattern(d+1) [ expr(d+1) ] expr(d+1) ")"
+pattern(d) = I(d) "(PatWildcard)" | I(d) "(PatBind l" uint ")" | I(d) "(PatInt " int ")"
+           | I(d) "(PatBool " bool ")" | I(d) "(PatStr " string ")" | I(d) "(PatChar " uint ")"
+           | I(d) "(PatRange " int " " int ")"
+           | I(d) "(PatVariant " id " " uint { pattern(d+1) } ")"
+           | I(d) "(PatTuple" { pattern(d+1) } ")" | I(d) "(PatOr" { pattern(d+1) } ")"
+```
+
+| Kind | Values | Flag | Children |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `IntLit` | the value in decimal | | |
+| `FloatLit` | the 16 lowercase hex digits of `to_bits` (5.1's) | | |
+| `BoolLit` | `true` or `false` | | |
+| `StrLit` | the string, quoted as 5.1 quotes it | | |
+| `CharLit` | the code point in decimal (5.1's) | | |
+| `Unit`, `Break`, `Continue` | | | |
+| `Local` | `l<n>` | | |
+| `MakeClosure` | the function's id | | `TypeArgs`; the captures |
+| `Call` | `Def <id>`, `Builtin <name>` (the Rust variant's name, as the resolution dump and N's `BUILTIN_VARIANTS` name it) or `Local l<n>` | | `TypeArgs`; the arguments |
+| `MakeVariant` | the sum's id, the variant's index | | the arguments |
+| `MakeRecord` | the record's id | | the fields, in declared order |
+| `MakeTuple`, `MakeArray`, `StrConcat` | | | the elements |
+| `FieldGet` | the index | | the target |
+| `FieldSet` | the index | | the target, the value |
+| `ArrayRepeat` | | | the value, the length |
+| `Index` | | | the target, the index |
+| `IndexSet` | | | the target, the index, the value |
+| `ArrayLen`, `ToStr`, `Await` | | | the operand |
+| `TraitCall` | the trait's id, the method's index | `receiver` | `SelfType`; `TypeArgs`; the receiver, when there is one; the arguments |
+| `Binary` | `Add` … `Shr` (`hir::BinOp`'s names) | | the two operands |
+| `LogicalAnd`, `LogicalOr` | | | the two operands |
+| `Unary` | `Neg`, `Not` or `BitNot` | | the operand |
+| `Let`, `Assign` | `l<n>` | | the value |
+| `Block` | | `tail` | the statements, then the tail when there is one |
+| `If` | | `else` | the condition, the branch, then the other when there is one |
+| `While` | | | the condition, the body |
+| `Match` | | | the scrutinee, then each arm |
+| `Return` | | `value` | the value, when there is one |
+
+A pattern carries no span or type (`hir::Pattern` has none), so it prints
+one line per pattern, its sub-patterns a level deeper; a range prints as
+stored, both ends included (`1..3` is `1 2`). `TypeArgs` prints only when
+there are any. Locals print in `hir::Function::locals`' order, `l<n>`
+their index; a closure's are its own, captures first. A flag is a
+`key=bool` field, so the harness's form check sees both of its values.
+
+`nova_typeck::dump::BODY_KINDS` lists every form a function prints; the
+harness checks that the full dumps of std, the corpus and the cases print
+each of them and nothing unlisted; 5.3a's `KINDS` stay the item part's.
+
+**One example of every form**, S0's `nova check --dump-hir forms.nova`
+of the source after it:
+
+```

+
+The closure `closure$u7` is `u7`: the program has seven definitions
+(`StdStart … def=7`), and its first closure prints as though it came
+right after them (§3), its `DefId` being past every definition, std's
+included. std's part prints its own closures as `s<n>` past std's
+definitions: natively `"fnval$s713"` is its first.
+
+**Sizes** (S0, 2026-11-13, at `5a9bd2d3`, a split of this branch for its
+plan whose code is this branch's, byte for byte): std's part natively
+24,066 lines (1,035,157 bytes), 681 functions; for the WASM target 24,848
+(1,048,056), 708; under test mode 24,137 (1,037,959), 684; 5.3a's item
+part was 3,107 lines natively. The corpus, natively: the 251 loose
+programs 78,316 lines (3.30 MB), 44 package files 93,189 (4.00 MB), N's
+44 package roots, each of which holds all of N, 1,886,009 (86.4 MB); the
+39 WASM programs 9,825 (0.42 MB); the 13 files with tests, under test
+mode, 440,672 (20.1 MB). Part 1, on `e5c555d0` (2026-11-12), measured
+the same figures but N's, which had no bodies then: its 30 package roots
+690,269 lines (31.7 MB), and the 10 files with tests 164,793 (7.48 MB).
+
+### 3. Closure ids
+
+A closure or wrapper takes a `DefId` past every definition
+(`next_closure_def`, from `defs.len()`), std's included, so 5.3a's id rule
+printed a program's first closure as `s<n>`, and std's closures, numbered
+after the program's, moved with the program's closure count (the
+research's headline 4). S0's ids stay as they are (§1); the dump maps
+them:
+
+- the program's closures and wrappers are those lifted from the
+  program's bodies, `defs.len()` up to the first of std's (`Checked`
+  records where std's begin); the `k`-th prints `u<D+k>`, `D` the
+  program's definitions (`StdStart`'s `def`), as though they came right
+  after them;
+- std's, the rest, the `k`-th prints `s<S+k>`, `S` std's definitions, as
+  though they came right after std's;
+- a lifted function's name holds its printed id: `closure$u7`,
+  `fnval$s713`.
+
+So std's part is the same text in every program of a mode (the driver's
+`std_part_of_a_programs_check_is_std_part`, now with closures on both
+sides), and a program's closures print the same whatever std's size
+(`shared_bodies_check_what_the_full_check_does` checks a program against
+std with one more module). N maps its own ids the same way.
+
+**If wrong:** a closure lifted from a program's body while std's are
+checked, or the other way, would print in the wrong part. No check lifts
+across bodies: a closure or wrapper is lifted while its enclosing body is
+checked and finalized with it (`pending_closures`). The equivalence test
+(§4) and the std-part test would show it. The rule costs nothing at run
+time: two numbers in `Checked`.
+
+### 4. std's bodies, shared, and the fallback
+
+std's bodies are checked once per process and mode: `SharedItems::new`
+checks std alone in full, items and bodies, and shares nothing should
+either give a diagnostic. A program's shared check
+(`nova_typeck::check_program_shared`) reads std's tables (ADR 0055 §4),
+checks the program's bodies alone, and stops at the program's segment:
+std's bodies are std's part, which `--std` prints. Its closures take the
+ids the full check gives them (§1), and its diagnostics are the full
+check's, since std's bodies give none.
+
+**The bug, and the fallback:** method lookup scans every impl, with no
+filter by the traits in scope (`resolve_method_on`,
+`find_inherent_method`), so a program can change how std's bodies
+check. The research's probes: `trait Mine { fn
+flush(self) -> Int }` with `impl Mine for Stdout` gives E0015 inside
+std's `ui/ssr` (`stdout().flush()`); an inherent `impl Stdout { fn flush
+… }` gives nothing, and std's call then binds to the program's method;
+an inherent `Map::new` gives E0074 and 20 E0015s in std's bodies. **This
+is a bug in S0, recorded here and not fixed in 5.3b:** std's bodies
+should not see a program's impls. S0's behaviour is unchanged. The
+user's ruling (2026-11-12): when a program implements anything on a
+type it does not own ("a std type or a primitive"), the shared path
+checks std's bodies with that program in full, so the dump equals the
+full check byte for byte. So the shared path takes the full check
+(`nova_typeck::implements_on_a_type_it_does_not_own`) when a program has
+an impl, inherent or a trait's, whose self type is not one of its own
+records or sums: a primitive, an array, or one of std's types.
+
+**5.3b's own condition**, not the user's: the full check is taken too
+when the item passes collected fewer of the program's impls than it
+wrote. An impl whose self type they refuse, a tuple, a function type or
+a projection (E0010, E0900), is not collected, so no self type is left
+to test, and none of those is a type the program owns; the count is how
+the trigger sees such an impl. The full check is what the dump must
+equal, so taking it can only cost time, on a program that has an error
+already; an impl no table holds cannot change how std's bodies check, so
+no input prints otherwise today. The full check prints std's bodies'
+diagnostics among the program's, so the dump equals the full check's
+byte for byte.
+
+**Who takes it:** natively 78 roots: the corpus's six std files checked
+as programs (`std/{bytes,collections,core,fmt,json,strings}/lib.nova`),
+five programs
+(`tests/runtime/{generic_impls,hidden_trait_methods,method_generics,trait_assoc_fn,where_clauses}.nova`),
+64 of `cases/check/` (the research's twelve probes and the two the
+plan's fact-check added, §5, `cases/check/std_bodies_*`, which must take
+it, and 5.3a's, 5.2's and the body tests' impl cases) and three of
+`cases/resolve/`; for the WASM target one case, under test mode one
+(the driver's guard lists them; part 2
+corrected the count, which was taken before every case was in). A program
+that takes it costs a second resolution and a full check.
+
+**The guard:** the driver's
+`std_checked_once_dumps_what_std_checked_for_each_program_dumps` compares
+the shared and unshared full dumps over every corpus root and case of
+each mode, in order and reversed, checks that every `std_bodies_*` case
+takes the full check, and lists those that do (78 natively, 76 at part
+5 before §5's last two cases; one for the WASM target, one under test
+mode). Parts 1 to 4 compared 5.3a's item dumps too; part 5 dropped
+them with the item-only dump (§10):
+the full dump holds the item tables, and on a root that takes the full
+check the shared item tables are built and set aside, printed nowhere.
+The unshared pass, which keeps nothing from one root to the next, runs
+in three parts on threads of its own beside the shared path's forward
+and backward passes (in the prototype, on `e5c555d0`, 95 s locally in
+one thread and 47 s so; 51.5 s at `5a9bd2d3`, 2026-11-13).
+
+### 5. The body cases
+
+The type checker's 426 body-level tests (the 550 that lex a source, less
+5.3a's 112 and the language server's 12 probe tests), with 724 sources,
+become cases by 5.3a's rule (ADR 0055 §5): the research's instrumentation
+of the test helpers (`r53b_rec`, a script, not committed) writes each
+source a test lexes under its name; a test's key is `check__<test>` for
+`check.rs`'s tests and `<module>__<test>` for `lang_tests`,
+`pattern_tests`, `std_tests` and `tuple_tests`; a case is `<key>.nova`,
+or `<key>_<k>.nova` for a test that lexed more than one source, `k` the
+source's place; the two-module test is a directory, `main.nova` and
+`lex.nova`; a source holding `@test` goes under test mode. A source whose
+text is a loose case's already (`check*` and `resolve*` of its mode) or
+an earlier source's is dropped: 77, which leaves 36 tests with no case of
+their own. That gives 641 files and one directory under `cases/check/`
+and four files under `cases/check-test/`; with 5.3a's 164, the twelve
+probes of §4 and one hand case for a fix of every kind of name
+(`body_fixes_for_every_need`), `cases/check/` held 819 programs. Three
+more by hand came of the plan's mutants (2026-11-13), each reaching
+sites no other input reached: `bodies_rare_forms_and_sites` (`~`, a
+record literal's unknown field, an associated function two bounds of a
+type parameter provide, a closure's declared return type, a variant of
+another sum in a pattern, E0060's note on `self`),
+`bodies_inference_variables_after_try_and_index_writes` (`?N` after a
+closure's `?` and after an index write) and
+`bodies_witnesses_of_strings_ranges_and_bools` (E0022's witnesses of a
+string and of ranges, E0020's `true` before `false`). Two more came of
+the plan's first fact-check (2026-11-13), beside §4's probes, each an
+impl the fallback's trigger must catch: `std_bodies_option_inherent`, an
+inherent `unwrap_or` on `Option`, std's first definition, that takes no
+argument where std's takes one, and `std_bodies_string_inherent`, an
+inherent `len` on `String` that takes one where std's takes none; each
+gives E0016 at std's calls (12 and 24), which only the full check
+prints: `cases/check/` holds 824 programs, 831 cases in all. Every
+one of the 38 codes occurs among them (the sixteen body codes that had
+no case before, E0011 … E0103, all through the extracted sources), and
+every note, secondary label and fix form occurs in the cases, the corpus
+or std.
+
+**Rust-only** (49): the 12 probe tests; `infer.rs`'s 13 and
+`usefulness.rs`'s 14; the builtin tables' 6
+(`builtin_signatures_are_what_the_std_call_sites_use`,
+`reserved_type_names_is_exactly_the_seven_expected_names`,
+`shutdown_requested_is_std_only_and_returns_bool`,
+`the_file_builtins_are_std_only_and_return_status_words`,
+`the_process_builtins_are_std_only_with_their_signatures`,
+`the_stream_builtins_are_std_only_and_return_status_words`);
+`std_tests::an_arrays_head_is_array_whatever_its_element`,
+`tuple_tests::a_tuple_displays_as_written`; and `items.rs`'s 2. 5.3b adds
+two more: the order test (§1) and `items.rs`'s shared bodies (§4).
+
+### 6. The harness, S0's side (part 1)
+
+`selfhost.rs` gained `N_BODIES`, false in part 1. Until N checks bodies,
+every comparison with N takes S0's `check --dump-hir-items` (`hir_s0`),
+so 5.3a's checks hold as they did, and the full dump's sets run through
+S0 alone, through `run`: std's three parts, the corpus natively, for the
+WASM target and under test mode, and the cases with both line endings;
+each dump well formed (`assert_well_formed`: every line at its depth,
+the parentheses balanced), every form of `KINDS` and `BODY_KINDS` and
+each of the 38 codes present, std's parts free of a program's id. Part 5
+removed `N_BODIES` and compares every set byte for byte (§10).
+

+### 8. N's bodies, part by part (parts 2 to 5)
+
+N checks the program's bodies as S0 does, function by function:
+`infer.nova` (S0's `infer.rs`: plain substitution, the occurs check, `!`
+and the error type unifying with anything, a failed unification keeping
+the bindings it made), `typeck_body.nova` (the order of §1, a function's,
+a method's and a constant's body, blocks, finalizing with E0011, E0081,
+E0103 and the helpers `child_exprs`, `collect_captures`, `remap_locals`,
+`split_operand`), `typeck_expr.nova` (`check_expr`, `.await` with E0086
+and E0087, interpolation, paths, operators, arrays, indexing) and
+`typeck_call.nova` (calls, `builtin_signature` by the variant's name,
+variants); `fixes.nova` gains the `Need`s of a value, a callee and a
+qualifier. N's idioms, beyond ADR 0055's:
+
+- HIR's body types are in `hir.nova`; a `LocalId` is an `Int`. An `Expr`
+  is a record of kind, type and span, so finalizing and remapping rewrite
+  it in place (spec §4.2); a kind is a sum, whose payload is replaced, not
+  rewritten. Names `ast.nova` holds too carry `Hir` (`HirExpr`,
+  `HirFunction`, `HirPattern`); a kind's variant is `Ek` and its Rust name
+  (`EkCall`), a pattern's `Pat` and the dump's name.
+- `fresh` stands where S0 calls it, in the same order, so `?N` numbers
+  alike; N's own tests pin a program's numbering.
+- A `Binding` is kept by its declaration's file label and span, and a
+  quiet newline split by its label, start and end, as S0 keeps them by
+  `Span`.
+- N checks the program's bodies, then std's, as S0's `check_bodies`
+  does (§1); the shared path stops after the program's (§4). Until part
+  4, N checked the program's alone and refused the rest.
+
+Part 3 adds the members: `typeck_method.nova` (record literals, fields
+and tuple elements, method lookup with `MethodRes`, method calls,
+`emit_inherent_call`, `emit_assoc_call`, `emit_trait_call` with
+`TraitCallSelf`, `qualifier_self_ty` and its `fresh` calls, interpolation
+through `Display` by `try_display`, `shown_method`), `typeck_place.nova`
+(assignment, `place_root`, `require_mutable_place` with `MutTarget` and
+`PlaceRoot`, element and field sets and their compound forms),
+`typeck_closure.nova` (closures lifted and functions as values wrapped,
+each taking the next id past every definition in the order met, named
+`closure$<id>` and `fnval$<id>`, which the dump prints under §3's rule)
+and, in `typeck_call.nova`, `T::f(…)` through a bound, `Type::f(…)`,
+`core_sum` and `?`. `fixes.nova` gains a record literal's `Need`,
+`mutable_fix`, `immutable_note`, `field_fix` and `method_fix`. Beyond
+part 2's idioms:
+
+- `check_call`'s two longest arms (`T::f`, `Type::f`) and `check_try`'s
+  E0099 are functions of their own in N, called where S0's code stands.
+- A receiver's or a field initializer's AST travels beside its checked
+  form, in `TraitCallSelf` as in S0, so `place_root` walks the place as
+  written.
+- A lifted closure's locals are copies of the enclosing function's, as
+  S0's `clone`, since finalizing rewrites a local in place.
+
+**Until N checked every body** (`N_BODIES` false, parts 2 to 4; this
+paragraph is their record), `selfhost hir` checks
+the program's bodies and prints the full dump, and `selfhost hir
+--items` prints 5.3a's item part, which every 5.3a comparison takes (the
+harness's `n_hir`, beside S0's `--dump-hir-items`). A construct a later
+part ports is one stub in N, which records what it is: N then prints
+`UNPORTED` and why after the root's header and exits 3, so a half-checked
+body is never compared as though it were complete. The stubs, after
+part 4: views (part 5). Parts 2 and 3 also stubbed `match`, `for`,
+destructuring `let` and std's bodies (part 4). `crates/nova-cli/tests/selfhost/n_bodies.txt`
+lists the inputs whose full program part N gives, and
+`n_gives_the_full_dump_of_the_listed_inputs_and_refuses_the_rest` holds it
+both ways over every input of the full dump's sets, std's three parts
+listed as `<mode> std` since part 4: each listed input's part is S0's,
+byte for byte, and every other input is one N refuses. Since part 4 the
+test runs its batches on every core, N's own package roots three at a
+time, as one set's thread was its long pole. Each part adds the inputs it then gives; the last sets
+`N_BODIES`, and removes the list, the test, `UNPORTED` and both item-only
+forms.
+
+**Part 2's figures** (2026-11-12): of 1,204 inputs (826 cases of the
+three modes, 378 corpus roots of the three modes), N gives 384 (352
+cases, 32 corpus roots; 364 reach the type checker, 362 with functions,

+Part 4 adds control flow and patterns: `usefulness.nova` (S0's
+`usefulness.rs`: `Ctor`, the pattern as `UPat`, `MatchCx` with
+`naming_values`, `missing_value`), `typeck_pattern.nova` (`check_match`,
+the reachability and exhaustiveness glue with E0020, E0021 and its
+"remove the unreachable arm" fix, `render_witness`, `check_pattern` with
+its variant, tuple, or- and range patterns, and `patterns.rs`'s
+`PatState`, E0100, E0101, E0022, E0104 with its "did you mean" fix, the
+or-alternatives' E0021 and `restrict_or`), `typeck_for.nova` (`for` over
+a range, an array and an `Iterator`-shaped `next`, `LoopBind`,
+`let_pattern`) and the destructuring `let` in `typeck_body.nova`;
+`fixes.nova` gains a pattern's `Need`, `scrutinee_sum`, `remove_arm_fix`
+and lines.rs's `arm_removal`. std's bodies: `share_items` checks them
+once per process and mode, on the checker its tables come from, whose
+tables a body never changes, and shares nothing should they give a
+diagnostic (S0's `SharedItems::new`, which collects std's items a second
+time to check them); `selfhost hir --std-part` prints std's full part;
+a program the shared path cannot check (§4) is resolved again in full
+and checked with std's bodies, as S0's driver does. Beyond the earlier
+parts' idioms:
+
+- `UPat`'s variants carry `Up`, as `hir.nova`'s `HirPattern` holds
+  `PatOr` and `PatTuple`; an or-pattern's tree node is `(parent node,
+  parent alternative, alternatives)`, the parent -1 at the top.
+- A matrix's rows and a witness are built new wherever S0 clones a
+  slice, since a `Vec` is shared when passed.
+- A witness's `String` and `Char` print as Rust's `{:?}` does
+  (`debug_str`, `debug_char`): `\0`, `\t`, `\r`, `\n`, `\\` and the
+  quote escaped, a control character, a format character, a separator, a
+  private use and the commonest grapheme extenders (combining marks,
+  variation selectors, the zero-width non-joiner) as the code point's
+  escape. Rust's full `is_printable` and `Grapheme_Extend` tables are
+  not ported (a departure; no input holds another such character).
+- A `for` loop's hidden locals are made where S0 makes them, a range's
+  `__run` after its body, since their ids reach the dump.
+
+**Part 4's figures** (2026-11-12): std's full part is S0's, byte for
+byte, in the three modes, at the first run. Of 1,216 roots and std's
+three parts (826 cases of the three modes, 390 corpus roots of the three
+modes), N gives 1,159 (806 cases, 350 corpus roots, std's three parts),
+every fallback root among them, and refuses 60, all for views (20
+cases, 40 corpus roots); none differs from S0's. With CRLF line endings,
+the 814 loose cases of `cases/check/` give 795 and refuse 19 (views).
+2,059 mutants of the listed cases and corpus roots, aimed at the members
+and at `match`, patterns, `for` and destructuring `let`, the research's
+16 probes of §4, 13 hand cases of the three modes and a two-module
+case, and every input of the type, name, mutation, soup, depth and edge
+fuzzers: none differs.

+### 9. Inference variables in S0's order
+
+`fresh` stands in N where S0 calls it, in the same order: 19 sites in
+N (`typeck_call.nova` 5, `typeck_method.nova` 5, `typeck_expr.nova` 3,
+`typeck_pattern.nova` 3, `typeck_closure.nova` 2, `typeck_place.nova`
+1) against S0's 19 (`check.rs` 18, `patterns.rs` 1), each in the
+function it mirrors, at the place S0's stands, so a `?N` in a message
+and every type the dump prints number alike. N's own tests pin a
+program's numbering (`typeck_body_tests.nova`), and every input above
+compares them. **If wrong:** a call moved renumbers
+every later variable of that function; the dump, which prints a type on
+every node, shows it at the first node it reaches.

+body fuzzers' bases are read from the loose corpus's compared dump
+(`loose_hir`, once a run) rather than from an S0 run of their own; the
+cases of each mode are dumped once a run (`hir_cases`) for the corpus and
+CRLF tests; the forms are read on the thread that made each dump, each
+distinct line once. The 38-code assertion holds on the cases and the
+corpus alone, which is stronger than on the differential's inputs with
+the fuzzers' (spec §4.6); the fuzzers' counts are reported beside it.
+
+**Each check this part added, and what it guards** (for the plan's
+mutants): the views' comparison (any line of `typeck_view.nova`, through
+the cases' E0094 to E0097 and the corpus's components); the merged
+corpus test's `BODY_KINDS` and 38 codes (a form or a code no input
+reaches); `--dump-hir-items` refused as the base refuses it (the removed
+form left half in place); the depth test's body kinds and its check that
+only `items` and `optionals` give a diagnostic (a generator gone wrong,
+or N's stack); the body fuzzer's checked-only, per-seed count, body-E0001
+and floors assertions (a mutation that stops before the type checker, a
+seed that writes fewer inputs, an item E0001 counted as a body's, an
+aimed code no longer reached); the driver test's three unshared parts
+(the same comparisons as before, by parts).
+
+**Checks the plan's mutants added** (2026-11-13): a HIR dump's root
+names on one command line stay under `HIR_ARGS_LIMIT`, asserted on every
+system, and the limit twice over fits Windows' 32,767 characters, so
+Linux sees a root list that would not fit Windows'; the depth test pins
+the levels of `BODY_DEEP_KINDS` (128, or the parser's 64 and 127); and
+`n_checks_std_for_each_program_when_std_gives_a_body_diagnostic`, beside
+the item-diagnostic test, gives N a std whose bodies give an E0010, which
+N must then check for each program (a temporary directory of its own,
+`body-error-std`). Two cases (§5) reach the trigger's sums and
+primitives: an impl on `Option`, std's first definition, and one on
+`String`, each of which changes std's bodies' diagnostics.
+
+### 11. The body fuzzer
+
+`fuzz::body_mutate` (spec §4.6) mutates the type fuzzer's bases (loose
+corpus programs that import nothing and check clean) one to
+three times inside their functions' and methods' bodies, by the tokens
+there: an integer, a string or a `true` made a value of another type; an
+argument added to a call, or its last one dropped; a field or a method
+renamed (`fz_<name>`); a one-line `match` arm deleted; an integer given
+`?` or `.await` (outside an `async fn`); a `let mut` made `let`; a
+`let`'s annotation removed; `break` put first in a body; or one of
+`fuzz::BODY_ITEMS` appended, 26 functions each aimed at a code (the
+type checker's E0001 for a value and for a function, E0010, E0011,
+E0013, E0014, E0015, E0016, E0020, E0021, E0022, E0060, E0080, E0081,
+E0086, E0087, E0098, E0099, E0100, E0104), each name numbered from the
+input's own. A mutation that would not parse is skipped; none renames
+what an item declares, so every input reaches the type checker, which
+the test asserts. **Seeds 501, 502 and 503**, 40 inputs each, in one
+process a side. Counts over the fixed seeds: E0001 13 (all the body's,
+by their messages), E0010 28, E0011 25, E0013 7, E0014 31, E0015 4,
+E0016 33, E0020 25, E0021 4, E0022 4, E0060 12, E0080 15, E0081 14,
+E0086 11, E0087 3, E0098 11, E0099 9, E0100 2, E0103 4, E0104 7: every
+floor of two (E0001, E0010, E0011, E0013, E0014, E0015, E0016, E0020,
+E0021, E0060, E0080, E0098, E0099) holds. The type fuzzer, now on the
+full dump: E0001 32, E0010 28, E0011 13, E0012 53, E0013 5, E0015 10,
+E0070 21, E0071 18, E0072 15, E0073 14, E0074 18, E0076 5, E0077 20,
+E0078 21, E0105 9, E0403 23, E0900 48. Among the cases and the corpus
+every one of the 38 codes occurs, as the corpus test prints them (E0087,
+E0095 and E0098 once each, E0073, E0086 and E0094 twice; E0001 906
+times).
+
+### 12. The depth cases, and N's stack
+
+`n_checks_128_levels_of_every_kind_on_a_1_mb_main_thread` runs N's
+`selfhost hir` on 45 programs under `ulimit -s 1024` (Linux, macOS; on
+Windows the main thread as it is), its dump S0's: 5.3a's ten written
+nestings of a type in all twelve item positions; every kind of
+`fuzz::DEEP_KINDS` at 128 levels (parentheses, blocks, `if`, `else if`,
+`match`, `while`, `for`, calls, prefix and binary operators, postfix
+chains, types, optionals, patterns, nested items, and a mixed one); and
+`fuzz::BODY_DEEP_KINDS` at the deepest level the parser takes: closures
+in closures, called at once, capturing and with parameters (64), arrays,
+indexing, tuples, interpolation, method chains, `?`, a `let`'s
+annotation, or- and `let` patterns, `match` in an arm and as a scrutinee
+(128), tuple and variant patterns in a `match` arm and `for` over a
+range, an array and with a tuple pattern (127). **Why not 128:** a
+closure called at once, `(|| e)()`, is two of the parser's levels, its
+parentheses and the closure, so 64 closures are 128 levels; a `match`
+arm's pattern starts a level in, the arm's own, so 127 patterns nest
+there; 127 `for` loops nest around the statement in the innermost, a
+level of its own. Every program reaches the type checker and none but
+`items` and `optionals` (E0900) gives a diagnostic. **N passes every
+one on 1 MB on both runtimes**; nothing overflows, so answer 2's
+departure is not needed here (ADR 0055 §12's normalized type stays the
+one recorded).
+
+Least stack (Linux, `ulimit -s`, 4 KB bisection, each run's dump
+compared with S0's, 2026-11-12):

+### 15. Departures from the spec, and decisions it does not settle
+
+- **(differs) The closure-id rule** (§3) is the dump's: a program's
+  closures print `u<D+k>` and std's `s<S+k>`, and the names hold the
+  printed id (`closure$u7`), where spec §4.1 says "`u<n>`, names as they
+  are". S0's own ids and symbols are §1's.
+- **(differs) The depth cases** reach 128 written levels but for
+  closures (64), patterns in a `match` arm and `for` loops (127), by the
+  parser's count (§12).
+- **(differs) The 38-code assertion** holds on the cases and the corpus
+  alone, not on the differential's inputs with the fuzzers' (§10):
+  stronger.
+- **(differs) Witnesses' strings and characters** approximate Rust's
+  `{:?}` (§8, part 4).
+- **(differs) 5.3a's item-only dump** (`check --dump-hir-items`) existed
+  only while 5.3b was built and is gone; the full dump holds the item
+  part, and the driver's equivalence test compares the full dumps alone
+  (§4).
+- **(differs) The Selfhost job builds S0 at `opt-level = 1`**
+  (`CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_OPT_LEVEL=1`, §14): CI past the lines went to the
+  user (answer 3), who chose it over a coverage cut (answer 6).
+- **N checks std's bodies on the checker its tables come from**, where
+  S0 collects std's items a second time (part 4); the fallback re-resolves
+  a program in full on both sides (§4).
+- **The body fuzzer's bases** are the type fuzzer's, now read from the
+  full dump, so a base checks clean in its bodies too; the type fuzzer's
+  inputs changed with it (its floors hold).
+
+### 16. The rule
+
+From 5.3b the whole type checker exists twice, in `nova-typeck` and in
+`selfhost/`: a change to either (a pass, the order of bodies, a
+diagnostic's words, order, notes, labels or fixes, a `fresh` call, a HIR
+node, std's sharing or its fallback) changes both in one pull request,
+and the full dump's differential (§10) holds them equal (phase plan
+decision 6, ADR 0055 §14 extended). The dump's grammar (§2) changes with
+them, on both sides.
+
+## Consequences
+
+- 5.4 starts from the HIR the full dump shows, the same on both sides
+  for every input the differential holds.
+- `selfhost.rs` doubles locally on the release runtime (21 to 45 s);
+  on CI, with S0 built at `opt-level = 1` in the Selfhost job (the
+  user's answer, §14), it took 48.78, 42.81 and 62.28 s, under the lines.
+- The bug of §4 (std's bodies see a program's impls) stays in S0, worked
+  around by the fallback, to be fixed later in both compilers at once.
+- N on a 1 MB stack meets the depth cases with room (at most 224 KB),
+  and the debug runtime's pauses stay under half a second.

+**Amended 2026-11-13 (branch `claude/loving-archimedes-frtf5q-53b`, ADR
+0056):** the bodies come in a fixed order: the program's functions, then
+its methods by their ids, which is their declaration order, then its
+constants, and then std's in the same order; the constant cycles (E0081)
+and the newline splits (E0103) follow, and the closures and wrappers are
+lifted in the order met, the program's before std's. Inference variables
+are numbered in the order the checker makes them, which `?N` in a
+message shows. The self-hosted compiler checks the bodies in the same
+order, word for word (5.3b, `selfhost hir`, compared with
+`nova check --dump-hir`'s full dump).
+
 ---
 
 ## 3. Core Type Representation

  `names.py` compares Task 0's list with this one binary by binary, by
  name: a binary is its `Running` or `Doc-tests` line, its hash stripped,
  an integration test's prefixed with the crate whose unit tests cargo
  listed just before it; a test is a line ending `: test`. Write it
  before the run, as the replay ran it:

```sh
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$P/plan53b/names.py")"
cat > "$P/plan53b/names.py" <<'EOF'
"""Compare two `cargo test --workspace -- --list` outputs binary by binary:
a binary is its `Running`/`Doc-tests` line, hash stripped; a test is a line
`NAME: test`. An integration test binary is named after the crate whose
unit tests cargo listed last before it, so two crates' `tests/tuples.rs`
stay apart. Prints each binary's count, and every name added or removed."""
import collections
import re
import sys


def tests(path):
    out = collections.OrderedDict()
    binary = None
    crate = ["?"]

    def binary_name(m, d):
        if d:
            return f"doc-tests {d.group(1)}"
        if m.group(1).startswith("unittests"):
            crate[0] = m.group(2)
            return f"{m.group(2)} ({m.group(1)})"
        return f"{crate[0]}: {m.group(1)} ({m.group(2)})"

    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
        m = re.match(r"\s+Running (.+?) \(target/debug/deps/(.+)-[0-9a-f]{16}\)", line)
        d = re.match(r"\s+Doc-tests (\S+)", line)
        if m or d:
            binary = binary_name(m, d)
            out.setdefault(binary, [])
            continue
        t = re.match(r"(.+): (test|bench)$", line.rstrip("\n"))
        if t and binary is not None:
            out[binary].append(t.group(1))
    return out


a, b = tests(sys.argv[1]), tests(sys.argv[2])
print(f"binaries: base {len(a)}, now {len(b)}")
print(f"tests: base {sum(map(len, a.values()))}, now {sum(map(len, b.values()))}")
added = 0
for k in list(a) + [k for k in b if k not in a]:
    if k not in a:
        print(f"binary added: {k}, {len(b[k])} tests")
        for t in b[k]:
            print(f"  + {t}")
        added += len(b[k])
        continue
    if k not in b:
        print(f"binary removed: {k}")
        continue
    ca, cb = collections.Counter(a[k]), collections.Counter(b[k])
    plus = sorted((cb - ca).elements())
    minus = sorted((ca - cb).elements())
    if plus or minus:
        print(f"{k}: {len(a[k])} -> {len(b[k])}, +{len(plus)} -{len(minus)}")
        for t in plus:
            print(f"  + {t}")
        for t in minus:
            print(f"  - {t}")
        added += len(plus) - len(minus)
print(f"net added: {added}")
EOF
```
